item.title: Joe Marchant recalled to England squad for training camp
item.description: Centre Joe Marchant won a recall to the England squad on Sunday after being included in a 36-player training camp for next month's Nations Championship, the Rugby Football Union announced.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Centre Joe Marchant won a recall to the England squad on Sunday after being included in a 36-player training camp for next month's Nations Championship, the Rugby Football Union announced. Marchant left to play in France after the 2023 World Cup but, having returned to play for Sale Sharks, is eligible again and part of a three-day camp as coach Steve Borthwick decides on his final selections for home tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, all at Twickenham. Uncapped trio Greg Fisilau, Archie McParland and Kepu Tuipulotu are all called up, although they have been in previous squads or training camps. Captain Maro Itoje returns after an extended break, while Fin Baxter and Will Stuart are back after injury left them out of previous selections. Chandler Cunningham-South and Benhard Janse van Rensburg miss out through injury, while veteran lock Courtney Lawes, back in England after a stint in France, has not been recalled. Squad Backs: Noah Caluori (Saracens), Fraser Dingwall (Northampton), George Ford (Sale), Tommy Freeman (Northampton), George Furbank (Harlequins), Will Joseph (Gloucester), Joe Marchant (Sale), Archie McParland, Alex Mitchell (both Northampton), Cadan Murley (Harlequins), Max Ojomoh (Bath), Henry Slade (Exeter), Fin Smith (Northampton), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Freddie Steward, Jack van Poortvliet (both Leicester) Forwards: Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ollie Chessum (Leicester), Arthur Clark (Gloucester), Alex Coles (Northampton), Luke Cowan-Dickie, Ben Curry, Tom Curry (all Sale), Ben Earl (Saracens), Greg Fisilau (Exeter), Jamie George (Saracens), Ellis Genge (Bristol), Joe Heyes (Leicester), Maro Itoje (Saracens), Emmanuel Iyogun (Northampton), George Martin (Saracens), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale), Tom Pearson, Henry Pollock (both Northampton), Will Stuart, Kepu Tuipulotu (both Bath).

item.title: Bayern Munich survive late scare to beat Freiburg 3-1 - Reuters
item.description: Bayern Munich survive late scare to beat Freiburg 3-1 Reuters

item.title: Bayern Munich survive late scare to beat Freiburg 3-1
item.description: Bayern Munich preserved their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season with a 3-1 victory at SC Freiburg, but the visitors were forced to withstand late pressure after Tom Bischof's own goal sparked a frantic push from the hosts for an equaliser.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich preserved their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season with a 3-1 victory at SC Freiburg, but the visitors were forced to withstand late pressure after Tom Bischof's own goal sparked a frantic push from the hosts for an equaliser. Bayern had been cruising at the Europa Park Stadion after taking an early lead when central defender Dayot Upamecano scored an unlikely opener in the 17th minute, sprinting forward through the middle on the counter-attack and latching on to a pass from Michael Olise before expertly slotting the ball past keeper Mio Backhaus. Freiburg, who got off to a superb start to the league season with four wins and a draw in their first five games before losing to Bayer Leverkusen, found themselves two down when winger Serge Gnabry surged down the left channel and finished from a tight angle three minutes before the break. The home side were thrown a lifeline when Bischof turned a pass from Rihito Yamamoto into his own net in the 82nd minute, but Olise restored his side's two-goal advantage deep into stoppage time to secure the win. Bayern are top of the table with 17 points from seven games, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference. Freiburg are third on 13 points. Earlier in the afternoon, Hoffenheim cruised to a 3-0 home win over Leverkusen but lost midfielder Alexander Prass to a late red card after he removed his shirt to celebrate scoring a goal. Facing the team fourth in the standings, Andrej Kramaric had given mid-table Hoffenheim the lead from the penalty spot in the 79th minute, and Prass all but wrapped up the three points for the home side by netting a second in the 89th minute. Forgetting that he had been booked on the stroke of half-time, Prass took off his shirt to celebrate and was horrified when he was shown a second yellow card before Max Moerstedt put the game beyond doubt with a third goal in the fifth minute of stoppage time.

item.title: Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” do Sul ao Nordeste; segundo Anac, aviação opera normalmente
item.description: A Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” saindo da região Sul para o Nordeste no último sábado, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A companhia aérea cancelou apenas um voo, que ia de Porto Alegre para Salvador.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” saindo da região Sul para o Nordeste no último sábado, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A companhia aérea cancelou apenas um voo, que ia de Porto Alegre para Salvador. “A companhia aérea Gol cancelou todos os voos de hoje, que iriam de parte do Sul do Brasil para o Nordeste”, dizem postagens no Instagram. A empresa informou em nota enviada à Reuters que o voo G31979, de Porto Alegre para Salvador marcado para o sábado, teve de ser cancelado por problemas técnicos com a aeronave. “Os clientes receberam as tratativas e foram reacomodados em outros voos da companhia”, afirmou. Segundo a assessoria da Gol, houve um voo extra após o ocorrido, e a aeronave pousou na capital baiana antes das 4h deste domingo. A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) declarou que “não há anormalidades no fluxo aéreo brasileiro” e que segue monitorando a movimentação. O órgão destacou que “atrasos e cancelamentos de voos fazem parte da rotina da aviação comercial”. De acordo com a agência, entre o sábado e este domingo de eleições, foram registrados outros três cancelamentos de voos para o Nordeste -- dois da Azul (um saindo de Brasília com destino a Recife, outro de Maceió também rumo à capital pernambucana) e um da Latam, de Guarulhos (SP) para Maceió.  A agência disse que entrou em contato com as três empresas para que informem as ações adotadas para realocar os passageiros.  O Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos também disse que está acompanhando a situação da aviação durante o pleito "para identificar prontamente eventuais problemas e assegurar a adoção das medidas necessárias para garantir o deslocamento dos eleitores". VEREDICTO Falso. A Gol cancelou somente um voo do Sul ao Nordeste neste fim de semana. Outras três viagens da Azul e da Latam para a região também foram suspensas. Segundo a Anac, a aviação brasileira está operando normalmente. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Report: Peyton Manning not expected to become Colts GM - Reuters

item.title: Report: Peyton Manning not expected to become Colts GM
item.description: Peyton Manning is not believed to be interested in the Indianapolis Colts' general manager job, and the team has not approached him about taking it, ESPN reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Peyton Manning is not believed to be interested in the Indianapolis Colts' general manager job, and the team has not approached him about taking it, ESPN reported Sunday. ESPN's sources said that the time commitment required to run an NFL front office would conflict with the Colts legend's post-playing projects -- Omaha Productions, the popular "Manningcast" with brother Eli as an alternative to ESPN/ABC's "Monday Night Football" telecasts, and his work as commercial spokesman. The Colts are looking for a new GM after firing Chris Ballard last week. Indianapolis began this season 2-4 after losing its final seven games in 2025. Ballard's teams were 72-82-1 during the regular season and 1-2 in the playoffs. The club last made the postseason in 2020. It did not win an AFC South division championships during Ballard's eight full seasons in charge. Manning said in 2024 that he was not focused on becoming a GM, but ESPN's sources noted that he is open to NFL opportunities, adding that they likely would need to be positions similar to the higher-level ones that former stars such as Tom Brady (Las Vegas Raiders part owner), Matt Ryan (Atlanta Falcons president of football operations) and Tony Boselli (Jacksonville Jaguars vice president of football operations) hold. Manning played 13 seasons for the Colts after being drafted No. 1 overall by Indianapolis in 1998. The Pro Football Hall of Famer threw for 54,828 yards and 399 touchdowns with the club. He was the QB when the Colts won Super Bowl XLI over the Chicago Bears in the 2006 season. After sitting out the 2011 season with shoulder and neck injuries, Manning was released by the Colts and signed with the Denver Broncos in 2012. He played four more seasons, retiring in 2015 after capturing a second Super Bowl ring that season, for Denver over the Carolina Panthers in Super Bowl 50. --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain will not join Canada's defence bank, source says - Reuters
item.description: Britain will not join Canada's defence bank, source says Reuters

item.title: Britain will not join Canada's defence bank, source says
item.description: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank, according to a source familiar with the matter, but the two countries said they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defence-funding initiatives.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank, according to a source familiar with the matter, but the two countries said they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defence-funding initiatives. In a statement on Sunday, the two governments said they had agreed to establish two distinct but complementary institutions to support each other on investment opportunities and strategic challenges. "We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives. We have agreed to develop a framework of cooperation that works in the interest of both institutions," the statement said. According to another source, the two governments were unable to agree on key issues including the location of the headquarters of the new bank, the level of joint procurement, lending to members, and the rules around new members joining in the future. The source said the MDM will focus on accelerating defence investment, joint procurement through financing, and bringing together demand across NATO allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defence industries and supply chains, focusing more on single sovereign lending. The DSRB has faced challenges securing support from larger European nations. Britain has previously distanced itself from the project. Britain and Canada said the MDM and DSRB will be designed to work in close partnership, so they can support each other on emerging industrial priorities, investment opportunities and strategic financing challenges.

item.title: Rennes go top of Ligue 1 with 3-0 win over Strasbourg
item.description: Rennes moved top of the Ligue 1 standings with a comprehensive 3-0 home triumph over RC Strasbourg on Sunday, moving one point ahead of Lille and AS Monaco, who drew earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rennes moved top of the Ligue 1 standings with a comprehensive 3-0 home triumph over RC Strasbourg on Sunday, moving one point ahead of Lille and AS Monaco, who drew earlier in the day. Sebastian Szymanski scored a double for Rennes, who advanced to 16 points from eight games, with Boulaye Dia opening the scoring in a comfortable triumph. Lille and Monaco are level on 15 points after they played out a 1-1 draw in the Principality, with Ethan Mbappe opening the scoring in the 24th minute as Lille imposed their early dominance. New Monaco coach Filipe Luis switched things around with a bevy of changes for the second half and, following Tanguy Nianzou's dismissal in the 66th minute, Edan Diop equalised in the 74th minute. Champions Paris St Germain and Olympique Lyonnais are next in the standings with 14 points and will play in the capital on Monday. The clash at the Parc des Princes was moved from Sunday to Monday after police raised security concerns ahead of weekend protests that had hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marching on Saturday. Largely peaceful rallies gave way to clashes as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of last week's unrest. Also on Sunday, there was a 4-3 home triumph for beleaguered Olympique de Marseille over Le Havre, helping them move up the league ladder after being stuck in the relegation zone just weeks ago. They are now eighth with 12 points, although it was a nerve-wracking affair for home fans before Marseille secured a third consecutive league victory. Le Havre had a penalty claim for possible handball seven minutes into stoppage time at the end of the game waved away after a VAR review. Marseille had led 4-0 in the 55th minute but nearly threw it away as Le Havre fought back to 4-3 with one minute to go. Le Havre remain bottom with two points from their first eight games of the season, three points adrift of Troyes, who picked up an away point in a goalless draw at Toulouse. There were also draws as Lorient were goalless away at Angers, while AJ Auxerre were held 1-1 at home by Le Mans.

item.title: Takeda to seek Japan approval for gastric cancer drug next year - Reuters
item.description: Takeda to seek Japan approval for gastric cancer drug next year Reuters

item.title: Takeda to seek Japan approval for gastric cancer drug next year
item.description: Takeda Pharmaceutical plans to seek regulatory approval in Japan next year for its gastric cancer drug, after it extended overall survival and delayed disease progression in a late-stage study, a company executive told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija
item.content:encoded: Takeda Pharmaceutical (4502.T) plans to seek regulatory approval in Japan next year for its gastric cancer drug, after it extended overall survival and delayed disease progression in a late-stage study, a company executive told Reuters. The drug, arcotatug tavatecan, or TAK-921, met both those main goals of the trial in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer who had received at least two prior therapies. "We will leverage this data and file in Japan with an NDA next year," PK Morrow, who leads oncology development for the Japanese drugmaker, said in an interview on Saturday at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid, referring to a new drug application. Some analysts said the data was "a solid start" for Takeda's more focused strategy for its oncology ambitions. The company is prioritizing development in lung and chest cancers, blood cancers and gastric cancer. Median overall survival was 10.2 months for patients on the drug versus 6.9 months for those given doctor's choice of chemotherapy, a difference that was deemed statistically significant. Median progression-free survival, or the time it took for the disease to worsen, was 7.1 months for the Takeda drug versus 3.1 months in the control group, according to an independent review. For a majority of patients in the study, Takeda's drug was their third line of therapy, and for 30% of the patients it was a fourth or fifth treatment, Morrow said. "Despite the fact that patients were so sick, they were able to tolerate the therapy. And secondly, we were still able to show significant benefit," she said. About 47% of patients on the drug had serious side effects, compared with about 56% of those on chemotherapy. The most common was low red blood cell count, or anemia, which affected about 20% of patients on the drug versus about 13% on chemotherapy. The data from the study of 464 patients from Japan and China was presented on Friday at the ESMO meeting. Severe nausea, vomiting and diarrhea were also less frequent with the Takeda drug, but one patient on the drug died suddenly from an unknown cause that was linked to the treatment, the company said. Takeda's drug targets a protein found on the surface of certain cancer cells called claudin 18.2, which was used as a biomarker for selecting patients most likely to benefit. The medicine belongs to a class of therapy known as antibody-drug conjugates. It delivers the cancer-killing agent exatecan directly to tumor cells. Takeda's trial enrolled patients with at least 75% of tumor cells expressing the target protein, but Morrow said the drug could be tested in patients with lower levels, given its tolerability profile. A rival drug from AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , which targets the same protein, [USN:L4N4691TE TEXT:"met the overall survival goal"] in a global study but did not show benefit on progression-free survival. Takeda licensed its drug from partner Innovent (1801.HK) , which holds rights to the medication in China.

item.title: Roche afirma que divarasib redujo riesgo de muerte en 44% en ensayo clínico sobre cáncer de pulmón
item.description: La farmacéutica suiza Roche anunció el domingo que su fármaco experimental contra el cáncer de pulmón divarasib redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 44% en comparación con los tratamientos actuales, según un estudio de fase III.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La farmacéutica suiza Roche (ROPC.S) anunció el domingo que su fármaco experimental contra el cáncer de pulmón divarasib redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 44% en comparación con los tratamientos actuales, según un estudio de fase III. • Roche señaló que los pacientes con cáncer de pulmón no microcítico con mutación KRAS G12C que habían recibido tratamiento previo y a los que se les administró divarasib presentaron una supervivencia global media de casi 18 meses, frente a los 12 meses de aquellos tratados con sotorasib o adagrasib • El divarasib también redujo el riesgo de progresión de la enfermedad o de muerte en un 42%, con una supervivencia media sin progresión de 9,8 meses frente a los 5,7 meses del grupo de control • El ensayo de fase III Krascendo 1 contó con la participación de 338 pacientes y comparó el divarasib con los dos inhibidores de KRAS G12C ya autorizados • La tasa de respuesta objetiva fue del 58% con divarasib, frente al 32% con sotorasib o adagrasib • No se observaron nuevos hallazgos en materia de seguridad. Alrededor del 4,8% de los pacientes tratados con divarasib interrumpieron el tratamiento debido a acontecimientos adversos relacionados con el mismo, frente al 11,7% del grupo de control • Los resultados se presentaron en el Congreso de la Sociedad Europea de Oncología Médica y se publicaron en la revista New England Journal of Medicine

item.title: Marine Le Pen anuncia candidatura a la presidencia de Francia mientras protestas sacuden el país
item.description: La líder de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen, favorita para las elecciones presidenciales francesas del año que viene, lanzó oficialmente su campaña el domingo con la promesa de restablecer el orden y la confianza nacional.
item.dc:creator: Lafken Zepeda, Nicolas Economou
item.content:encoded: La líder de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen, favorita para las elecciones presidenciales francesas del año que viene, lanzó oficialmente su campaña el domingo con la promesa de restablecer el orden y la confianza nacional. Mientras Francia se enfrenta a uno de sus períodos más turbulentos de los últimos años, Le Pen se presentó como la mejor opción para capear lo que describió como crecientes crisis económicas, sociales y de seguridad. "No estamos viviendo el fin del mundo, sino el fin de un mundo, su mundo", afirmó refiriéndose a sus oponentes políticos. Le Pen eligió pronunciar su primer discurso de campaña en Orleans, cuna de Juana de Arco, la heroína del siglo XV venerada por los nacionalistas como símbolo de patriotismo y soberanía. Dirigiéndose a una multitud de seguidores que la aclamaban, prometió una política de "tolerancia cero" y afirmó que restablecer la seguridad era el primer deber del Estado. Las protestas masivas por el costo de vida y la desigualdad del pasado fin de semana degeneraron en saqueos y actos de vandalismo. Los disturbios callejeros han dado un impulso a Le Pen y una encuesta de opinión publicada el domingo la sitúa entre el 32% y el 33,5% de las preferencias, muy por delante de su rival más cercano, el líder de la extrema izquierda Jean-Luc Mélenchon, con un 17%, a medida que los votantes abandonan los partidos mayoritarios para decantarse por los extremos políticos. Las encuestas sugieren que derrotaría fácilmente a Mélenchon en una segunda vuelta, que se prevé que se celebre a principios de mayo. En un intento por transmitir optimismo, Le Pen centró su discurso en el tema de un "renacimiento" nacional. Afirmó que Francia atraviesa un período de agitación, pero que saldría fortalecida si adoptara su visión de seguridad, prosperidad y renovación. Le Pen prometió mano dura en materia de inmigración, comprometiéndose a restablecer los controles fronterizos, expulsar automáticamente a los delincuentes extranjeros y tomar medidas enérgicas contra las bandas y los traficantes de drogas. La propia Le Pen podría verse obligada a hacer campaña con una tobillera electrónica tras haber sido condenada por malversación de fondos del Parlamento Europeo. Ha recurrido la sentencia judicial. En materia económica, Le Pen se comprometió a aplicar medidas de austeridad, reducir los impuestos a las empresas, recortar la burocracia y apoyar a la industria, la innovación y la inteligencia artificial. Rechazó nuevos aumentos de la edad de jubilación.

item.title: UK's Burnham says he is open to discussing EU free movement
item.description: Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

UK's Burnham says he is open to discussing EU free movement

Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham speaks as he delivers a speech during the The Innovation Nation Summit at Bruntwood SciTech on Oct 9, 2026, in Manchester. (File photo: Pool via Reuters/Christopher Furlong)

FAST

LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc. Building on previous comments about the need to rethink ties with Brussels, Burnham told the Sunday Times that the influx of EU workers into Britain before Brexit had posed very significant challenges. "But, at the same time, it was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he said. "Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different. The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we’ve just got to have an honest discussion about those things." Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

In September, two months after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour Party leader and prime minister, Burnham said Britain should consider options for its relationship with the EU, including possibly rejoining the bloc one day. He had previously backed the pledges of Starmer's government which included no return to freedom of movement which Brussels sets as a condition for being part of the bloc's single market. In his interview with the Sunday Times, conducted on Oct 19, Burnham said the issue of freedom of movement could be considered as part of a broader reset of Britain's relationship with the EU, including on data sharing and migration.

Related:

Burnham hopes for EU deal next month, stirs Brexit debate

'Welcome back,' says Macron, as UK PM opens door to EU return

"You've got to see it in the round, rather than just looking at freedom of movement on its own," he said. Burnham, who is trying to find ways to speed up Britain's economy, is due to meet top EU officials for a summit on Nov 20. He said he could not imagine recommending that Britain adopt the euro currency or the EU's border-free travel arrangements. A new referendum would be needed to rejoin the EU but not necessarily to join the bloc's single market or a customs union, the Sunday Times quoted Burnham as saying. Former Conservative finance minister Jeremy Hunt, who campaigned to stay in the EU in 2016, said it would be a mistake to reopen one of the fundamental debates of the referendum and he said relaxing immigration rules would hurt people in Britain. "I think it will be a hammer blow to getting people off welfare and into work," Hunt told Sky News.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: United leave Carrick hanging by a thread after Bournemouth loss
item.description: Michael Carrick insisted he was "carrying on as normal" after Manchester United's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday, but the manager appeared increasingly vulnerable after a result that left Old Trafford engulfed in anger and resignation.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick insisted he was "carrying on as normal" after Manchester United's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday, but the manager appeared increasingly vulnerable after a result that left Old Trafford engulfed in anger and resignation. Asked if he expected to still be in charge next week, Carrick offered no guarantees. "Of course, I take responsibility," he said. "Whatever's going to happen, results-wise, whether we win, we lose, draw, whatever happens ... the responsibility is mine." Pressed on whether he expected to be sacked in the coming days, Carrick said: "I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I'm carrying on as normal, and I love this place. "I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really." While Carrick led a resurgent United to third place last season after replacing Ruben Amorim, they have won only twice in 12 matches this campaign across all competitions, and have not won in the top flight since they defeated newly promoted Ipswich Town on August 30. Sunday's defeat left them with seven points from eight league matches, and just a point above the drop zone, their worst return at this stage of a season since 1986-87. Supporters unfurled a giant banner reading "Standards" before halftime featuring club icons Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson. The fans largely reserved their sympathy for Carrick, singing "It's Carrick you know!" late in the game. But once the 45-year-old tapped a hand to his heart and disappeared down the post-game tunnel, those chants gave way to loud boos directed at the players. The manner of the defeat was almost as damaging as the scoreline. Bournemouth supporters repeatedly taunted Carrick with chants of "You're getting sacked in the morning", while thousands of United fans streamed towards the exits before the final whistle. Former United winger Ashley Young said the performance suggested the squad was no longer responding to its manager. "The fans are behind him and backing him because he's a legend of the football club," Young said on the Sky Sports broadcast. "But the players on the pitch showed nothing. They didn't run, they didn't look like a team together. You could tell today that it was like they'd given up." BRUNO LEFT OUT The pressure on Carrick was intensified by his decision to leave captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench four days after the Portugal midfielder publicly criticised United's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Carrick had insisted before kickoff that omitting Fernandes was a "pure football" decision. Television cameras repeatedly caught the midfielder looking dismayed as United lurched towards another defeat. The third goal summed up the chaos. After United lost possession high up the pitch, goalkeeper Senne Lammens raced from his area but completely misjudged a long ball forward, allowing Evanilson to loft the ball into an unguarded net. It was United's afternoon in miniature: disorganised, fragile and punishingly exposed. Harry Maguire, who wore the captain's armband for the day, insisted Carrick had the full support of the dressing room. "We're fully behind Michael (Carrick)," Maguire said. "Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough." Carrick looked close to tears when asked about the supporters' backing after the match. "To be in such a difficult situation and go through a day like we have done and a spell like we have done is certainly difficult to take," he said. "So there's real mixed emotions in there for sure." He rejected suggestions his acknowledgement of supporters after the final whistle had been a farewell. "No, not from me ... just appreciation for the fans and what they've showed me." Former United defender Gary Neville said the crowd's support reflected a belief among fans that Carrick's fate had already been sealed. "The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what's going to happen here," Neville said. Even Bournemouth boss Marco Rose expressed sympathy for the beleaguered Manchester manager. "I feel a lot of empathy for my colleagues," he said. "We are just humans, and we try to do our job the best possible way. At the end, it's never easy for us, and I feel with Michael."

item.title: Roche says divarasib cut risk of death 44% in lung cancer trial - Reuters
item.description: Roche says divarasib cut risk of death 44% in lung cancer trial Reuters

item.title: Roche says divarasib cut risk of death 44% in lung cancer trial
item.description: Swiss drugmaker Roche said on Sunday its experimental lung cancer drug divarasib reduced the risk of death by 44% compared with existing treatments in a phase III study.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss drugmaker Roche (ROPC.S) said on Sunday its experimental lung cancer drug divarasib reduced the risk of death by 44% compared with existing treatments in a phase III study. • Roche said patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer who received divarasib had median overall survival of nearly 18 months, compared with 12 months for those treated with sotorasib or adagrasib • Divarasib also lowered the risk of disease progression or death by 42%, with median progression-free survival of 9.8 months against 5.7 months in the control group • The Phase III Krascendo 1 trial involved 338 patients and compared divarasib with the two approved KRAS G12C inhibitors • The objective response rate was 58% for divarasib, versus 32% for sotorasib or adagrasib • No new safety findings were observed. Some 4.8% of patients on divarasib stopped treatment because of treatment-related adverse events, versus 11.7% in the control group • Roche said it was working with health authorities to bring the treatment to patients • The results were presented at the [USN:L2N46B04N TEXT:"European Society for Medical Oncology Congress"] and published in the New England Journal of Medicine

item.title: Game 6 of WNBA Finals in Atlanta awaits arena decision
item.description: With the WNBA Finals now set to go at least six games, a venue for Game 6 in the series still needs to be decided.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: With the WNBA Finals now set to go at least six games, a venue for Game 6 in the series still needs to be decided. The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are tied 2-2 in the best-of-seven with Game 5 on Monday in San Francisco. The winner of that game can clinch the title in Game 6 on Thursday in Atlanta. With no schedule change, Game 6 could end up being played at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center, which is the regular home for Dream games. But Atlanta has been playing in the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena for its playoff games and sold out Games 3 and 4 of the Finals at the venue. On Thursday night, the NBA's Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to face the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena, creating a venue conflict. The WNBA handled arena scheduling conflicts for Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta with schedule changes for those games. Game 4 was moved to a 1 p.m. local start with the Hawks playing host to the Houston Rockets later in the day. With Game 5 on Monday and a potential Game 7 on Saturday, the league has options to change the date of Game 6. Because Game 6 is scheduled to be played on a weekday, a start-time change to create another WNBA/NBA doubleheader is not likely. According to Front Office Sports, a change in date is not as simple as the WNBA deciding it will happen. USA Network is set to broadcast Game 6 at 8 p.m. local time and must be agreeable to the change, according to the report, with the visiting Valkyries also having a say in any changes. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil polls: President Lula da Silva gets 1st smartphone at 80, but can he catch up with Brazil’s digital generation?
item.description: Brazilian President Lula da Silva has got his first smartphone at 80 as he steps up social media campaigning ahead of the presidential runoff. With digital-savvy rivals gaining ground, can the veteran leader connect with Brazil’s younger voters?
item.dc:creator: Bhanu Pratap
item.content:encoded: Just days before his 81st birthday, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva got a new smartphone — reportedly his first ever — as he steps up efforts to connect with voters through social media ahead of a closely watched presidential runoff.“I’m becoming the king of selfies, a real internet user,” Lula told supporters at a recent rally in Brasília, signalling a shift in how the veteran left-wing leader is approaching political campaigning.As Reuters reported, Lula’s smartphone debut comes at a time when social media platforms such as TikTok, Instagram and WhatsApp are increasingly shaping Brazil’s political landscape.The ability to build a large online following and convert digital influence into votes has become a powerful electoral asset, particularly for younger candidates.For Lula, who has spent decades building his political identity through trade unions, grassroots mobilisation and mass rallies, adapting to this new environment could prove crucial as he seeks an unprecedented fourth presidential term.Brazil’s political battle moves onlineThe growing influence of digital campaigning was evident in congressional elections held alongside the first round of this month’s presidential vote. Several younger candidates with strong social media followings performed exceptionally well, according to the report. Lula’s opponent in the runoff is right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.At 45, Flávio has been reaching voters through his own YouTube channel and has emerged as a formidable challenger after topping the first-round vote, surprising pollsters, Reuters reported. Lula learns the social media gameLula, a former shoeshine boy who went on to become a metalworker, trade union leader, and an internationally recognised left-wing politician, first ran for president in 1989. His political communication has historically relied on personal connections with workers, grassroots organisations and supporters at large public gatherings.Ana Elisa Silva, the 21-year-old law student from Minas Gerais, has joined Lula’s inner circle to help him navigate the social media landscape following his disappointing first-round performance, according to Reuters report.Silva told Reuters that the transition required adjustments for a politician who has openly acknowledged his dislike of mobile phones.“This experience remains important, but it needs to align with changes in how people consume information, especially young people.” The rise of ‘influencer politicians’The growing prominence of politicians who have built their own digital audiences marks a further evolution in electoral campaigning, according to Máximo Zaldívar, regional director for Latin America and the Caribbean at the International Foundation for Electoral Systems.Politicians once approached social media personalities to endorse their campaigns. Increasingly, however, candidates themselves are building audiences and political influence through their online content.“The influencer has their own political capital,” Zaldívar said, referring to the followings accumulated across platforms. “That’s what they bring to the table and no politician can compete with that.”Ferreira exemplifies this trend. A staunch Bolsonaro supporter and the son of an evangelical pastor, he has nearly 25 million Instagram followers — equivalent to more than 10% of Brazil’s population.Conservative lawmaker Julia Zanatta, 41, who has more than one million Instagram followers and won over half a million votes in this month’s election, said success on social media requires consistency and a willingness to communicate without being overly concerned about criticism.“I never thought about whether I’d reach more people or if I’d displease anyone,” she said, as per Reuters.With inputs from Reuters.

item.title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returns after first-half exit
item.description: San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey returned to open the second half after he departed in the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday with a thigh injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey returned to open the second half after he departed in the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday with a thigh injury. After catching three passes for 45 yards and rushing four times for 29 yards with a touchdown, McCaffrey exited before trainers worked on his left leg. He then jogged to the locker room for further examination while he was listed as questionable to return. The 10-year veteran sat out the 49ers' entire third drive, which ended with backup running back Kaelon Black's 30-yard rushing touchdown. The 49ers led 14-12 at halftime. McCaffrey had just one carry for minus-2 yards on San Francisco's first drive of the second half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marine Le Pen lança candidatura à presidência da França em meio a onda de protestos
item.description: A líder da extrema direita francesa, Marine Le Pen, favorita na corrida presidencial do próximo ano, lançou formalmente sua candidatura neste domingo prometendo restaurar a ordem e a confiança nacional.
item.dc:creator: Lafken Zepeda, Nicolas Economou
item.content:encoded: A líder da extrema direita francesa, Marine Le Pen, favorita na corrida presidencial do próximo ano, lançou formalmente sua candidatura neste domingo prometendo restaurar a ordem e a confiança nacional. Em um momento em que a França atravessa um de seus períodos mais turbulentos dos últimos anos, Le Pen se apresentou como a candidata mais preparada para enfrentar o que classificou como uma combinação crescente de crises econômica, social e de segurança. "Não estamos vivendo o fim do mundo, mas o fim de um mundo, o mundo deles", disse ela, em referência a seus adversários políticos. Le Pen escolheu fazer seu primeiro discurso de campanha em Orléans, cidade associada a Joana d'Arc, heroína guerreira do século XV reverenciada por nacionalistas franceses como símbolo de patriotismo e soberania. Diante de uma multidão de apoiadores, ela prometeu uma política de "tolerância zero" contra o crime e afirmou que restaurar a segurança é o principal dever do Estado. Os protestos em massa contra o aumento do custo de vida e a desigualdade social, realizados no fim de semana passado, terminaram em episódios de saques e vandalismo. PESQUISA COLOCA LE PEN NA LIDERANÇA A turbulência nas ruas parece ter beneficiado Le Pen. Uma pesquisa de opinião divulgada neste domingo mostrou a líder da extrema direita com entre 32% e 33,5% das intenções de voto, bem à frente de seu rival mais próximo, o líder da esquerda radical Jean-Luc Mélenchon, que aparece com 17%. O levantamento sugere que Le Pen derrotaria Mélenchon com facilidade em um eventual segundo turno, previsto para o início de maio. Em uma tentativa de transmitir otimismo, Le Pen estruturou seu discurso em torno do tema de uma "Renascença" nacional. Segundo ela, a França vive um período de profunda transformação, mas sairá mais forte se adotar sua visão baseada em segurança, prosperidade e renovação. "Nós dizemos: 'as coisas eram boas antes, serão melhores amanhã!'", afirmou. Le Pen prometeu endurecer as políticas de imigração, restaurar controles de fronteira, expulsar automaticamente estrangeiros condenados por crimes e intensificar o combate a gangues e traficantes de drogas. A própria Le Pen poderá fazer campanha usando uma tornozeleira eletrônica após ter sido condenada por desvio de recursos do Parlamento Europeu. Ela recorre da decisão judicial. ECONOMIA, EUROPA E UNIDADE PARTIDÁRIA Na economia, Le Pen prometeu contenção de gastos públicos, redução de impostos para empresas, menos burocracia e apoio à indústria, à inovação e à inteligência artificial. Também rejeitou novas elevações da idade mínima de aposentadoria. O congresso partidário foi planejado para demonstrar unidade na cúpula da legenda Reagrupamento Nacional. Jordan Bardella foi reeleito presidente do partido e apresentado como a escolha de Le Pen para o cargo de primeiro-ministro. O discurso de Bardella foi interrompido por ativistas de uma união estudantil judaica, que chamaram atenção para recentes acusações de que ele teria feito comentários antissemitas na juventude, acusações que ele nega. Le Pen passou mais de uma década tentando transformar o partido herdado de seu pai, Jean-Marie Le Pen, em 2011, suavizando sua imagem e ampliando seu apelo político para além da base tradicionalmente anti-imigração. Sobre a Europa, Le Pen evitou defender uma saída da França da União Europeia, mas afirmou que reduzirá a influência de Bruxelas, restaurará o controle nacional sobre fronteiras e leis e colocará os interesses franceses em primeiro lugar, incluindo evitar o envolvimento do país em guerras estrangeiras. "O futuro nos pertence", declarou, antes de liderar a multidão que agitava bandeiras francesas no canto do hino nacional. (Reportagem de Juliette Jabkhiro, Lafken Zepeda e Nicolas Economou)

item.title: Trump campaigns in Michigan a day after Obama rallies Democrats
item.description: Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow majorities.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump campaigns in Michigan a day after Obama rallies Democrats

Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow majorities.

Former President Barack Obama, joined by Democratic nominee for US Senate Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic gubernatorial nominee and Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, raise hands during a campaign event at Cass Technical High School, on Oct 24 2026, in Detroit. (Photo: AP/Paul Sancya)

FAST

DETROIT: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday (Oct 25), a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections.  Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests, an open-seat race between former Republican Representative Mike Rogers and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that will help decide control of the chamber. Despite repeatedly attacking El-Sayed from the Oval Office and at rallies across the country, the Republican president had not yet campaigned in Michigan this year.  If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist and repeatedly mocked his middle name, Mohamed, a common Muslim name.

El-Sayed has dismissed the accusation and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "Faith is a thing there’s just too little of in Washington." Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups.  "If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers said at a debate last week.  El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group and says it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States.

Related:

Trump's approval rating sinks to record low two weeks before midterm elections

Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms

At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks on El-Sayed as an attempt by opponents to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are".  The former president compared it to his experience as the target of false claims that he was born in Kenya. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul."  Trump's rally in Port Huron, part of an area of Michigan that he won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66 per cent of the vote, will also highlight the US-Canada tariff standoff.  The trade fight has affected the Detroit-based US auto industry, prompting Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy.  Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Thousands protest Czech government's public media overhaul after rushed vote - Reuters
item.description: Thousands protest Czech government's public media overhaul after rushed vote Reuters

item.title: Thousands protest Czech government's public media overhaul after rushed vote
item.description: Thousands protested in Prague on Sunday after government lawmakers gave initial backing to public media funding changes in a rare overnight vote despite criticism the overhaul will damage media independence.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands protested in Prague on Sunday after government lawmakers gave initial backing to public media funding changes in a rare overnight vote despite criticism the overhaul will damage media independence. The proposal's first reading was unexpectedly brought to the lower house floor outside the planned order of proceedings on Friday. Opponents and media advocacy groups have objected to fast-tracking the legislation, which will abolish household fees that currently fund Czech public television and radio stations. The populist government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis, backed by the far-right SPD party, has frequently clashed with public and private media. It wants to move funding for Czech Television and Czech Radio to the state budget, which critics say will leave broadcasters vulnerable to political pressure. GOVERNMENT HAS 'GONE TOO FAR', PROTEST LEADER SAYS Babis says it is a matter of funding transparency and not an attack on independence. Smaller protests first broke out on Friday at the bill's unexpected introduction. Speaker Tomio Okamura of the SPD limited debate and scheduled a vote for 4:36 a.m. (0336 GMT) on Saturday. The bill is now at the committee stage before a later vote. "Mr Babis ... Mr Okamura, nobody in this country believes that your intention was pure," Mikulas Minar, a protest leader, said on Sunday, criticising the overnight vote. "(This protest) is a clear message to this government: you have really gone too far this time," he told protesters who had filled Prague's historic Old Town Square, amid chants of "Resignation" and "We've had enough". Organisers plan further protests. TRUST HIGH IN PUBLIC MEDIA Czech Television is the country's most-watched broadcaster across major age groups. Public media are among the most trusted news sources in the country, according to a 2025 Reuters Institute survey. The proposal would cut funding for Czech Television and Czech Radio by about 15%, possibly as early as next year. Opposition parties have compared the funding changes with reforms in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, who oversaw a major expansion of pro-government media. On Friday, the European Broadcasting Union, along with 15 other groups including other public broadcasters as well as Reporters Without Borders, called for more debate and the removal of any measures threatening the broadcasters' financial sustainability. President Petr Pavel also called for more expert scrutiny. "The Czech Republic is among the few countries in central and eastern Europe where the system of public service and private media works very well," he said on X on Saturday.

item.title: France's Le Pen launches presidential bid as protests rattle the nation
item.description: Le Pen cast herself as the best placed to navigate mounting economic, social and security crises.
item.dc:creator: Lafken Zepeda, Nicolas Economou
item.content:encoded: Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner in next year's French presidential election, formally launched her campaign on Sunday with a promise to restore order and national confidence. As France faces one of its most turbulent periods in years, Le Pen cast herself as the best placed to navigate what she described as mounting economic, social and security crises. "We are not living through the end of the world but the end of a world, their world," she said of her political opponents. Le Pen chose to make her first campaign address in Orleans, home to Joan of Arc, the 15th-century warrior heroine revered by nationalists as a symbol of patriotism and sovereignty. Addressing a crowd of cheering supporters, she promised "zero tolerance" policing and said restoring security was the state's first duty. [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"Mass protests"] over living costs and inequality last weekend descended into looting and vandalism. OPINION POLL PUTS LE PEN IN THE LEAD The street turmoil has given Le Pen a boost and an opinion poll published on Sunday put her on 32% to 33.5%, well ahead of her nearest rival, hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon on 17%, as voters desert mainstream parties for the political extremes. Surveys suggest she would easily defeat Melenchon in a run-off ballot, expected to be held in early May. Seeking to project optimism, Le Pen built her speech around the theme of a national "Renaissance". She said France was living through a period of upheaval but would emerge stronger if it embraced her vision of security, prosperity and renewal. "We say: 'Things were good before, they will be better tomorrow!'," she said. Le Pen promised a hard line on immigration, pledging to restore border controls, automatically expel foreign criminals and crack down on gangs and drug traffickers. Le Pen herself could have to campaign wearing an ankle tag after she was [USN:L6N43A0U8 TEXT:"convicted of embezzling"] European Parliament funds. She is appealing the court verdict. On the economy, Le Pen pledged spending restraint, lower business taxes, reduced bureaucracy and support for industry, innovation and artificial intelligence. She rejected further increases in the retirement age. The congress was designed to showcase unity at the top of the National Rally party, with Jordan Bardella re-elected party president and presented as Le Pen's choice for prime minister. Bardella's speech was interrupted by activists from a Jewish student union, drawing attention to recent accusations he made [USN:L6N45T12D TEXT:"antisemitic comments"] in his youth, which he denies. Le Pen has spent more than a decade trying to transform the party she inherited from her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, in 2011, softening its image and broadening its appeal beyond its traditional anti-immigration base. On Europe, Le Pen stopped short of advocating a French exit from the European Union, but said she would roll back Brussels' influence, restore national control over borders and laws, and put French interests first, including avoiding foreign wars. "The future belongs to us," she said, before leading the flag-waving crowd in singing the national anthem.

item.title: Trump não pretende assumir controle de eleições estaduais, diz procurador-geral dos EUA
item.description: O esforço do Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos para bloquear preventivamente a certificação do resultado da eleição para o Senado no Estado do Alasca não tem como objetivo dar ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, controle sobre eleições estaduais, afirmou neste domingo o procurador-geral norte-americano, Todd Blanche.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O esforço do Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos para bloquear preventivamente a certificação do resultado da eleição para o Senado no Estado do Alasca não tem como objetivo dar ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, controle sobre eleições estaduais, afirmou neste domingo o procurador-geral norte-americano, Todd Blanche. O órgão comandado por Blanche entrou com uma ação na sexta-feira para impedir que o Alasca certifique o resultado da disputa para o Senado dos EUA caso o candidato republicano à reeleição seja derrotado por uma margem apertada. Mas, segundo Blanche, o Departamento de Justiça não está preparando terreno para reverter um resultado eleitoral desfavorável a Trump. "O presidente Trump não está tentando assumir o controle de uma eleição estadual de forma alguma", disse Blanche ao programa "State of the Union", da CNN. "Não estamos criando as bases para que o presidente faça isso." Autoridades eleitorais de todo o país disseram à Reuters que estão se preparando para possíveis interferências federais nas eleições legislativas de 3 de novembro, que definirão o controle do Congresso dos EUA. Entre as preocupações estão contestações judiciais e disputas sobre a votação que possam atrasar ou impedir a certificação dos resultados. Além do processo contra o Alasca, o governo Trump adotou outras medidas relacionadas ao sistema eleitoral dos Estados, incluindo uma ação judicial para impedir a Califórnia de contabilizar determinadas cédulas enviadas pelo correio e uma tentativa, em grande parte malsucedida, de obrigar 30 Estados e o Distrito de Columbia a fornecerem listas completas de eleitores. Blanche afirmou que a ação referente ao Alasca diz respeito especificamente àquele Estado e reiterou o argumento do governo Trump de que os eleitores podem ficar "confusos" porque dois republicanos na cédula têm nomes quase idênticos: o senador em exercício Dan S. Sullivan e o desafiante Dan J. Sullivan Jr.. Segundo Blanche, o segundo candidato concorre apenas "para confundir os eleitores". "Nunca antes adversários chegaram a tais extremos para tentar sabotar e fraudar uma eleição como neste caso", afirmou Blanche à CNN. Dan J. Sullivan tem negado, em entrevistas à imprensa norte-americana, que sua candidatura tenha o objetivo de causar confusão ou desviar votos de Dan S. Sullivan. Sua campanha não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Blanche disse que a ação judicial foi apresentada para dar às autoridades "a capacidade de determinar se houve confusão que viole a lei". Ele se recusou a comentar se Trump ordenou que apresentasse o processo, embora o próprio presidente tenha afirmado que o fez. Trump voltou a comentar o caso do Alasca neste domingo, acusando os democratas de orquestrarem a candidatura de Dan J. Sullivan. "Eles tornaram tudo muito confuso e acho isso muito injusto", disse Trump a jornalistas antes de embarcar para o Estado de Michigan. "Acho que é ilegal porque é injusto. Você quer justiça nas eleições." Críticos da iniciativa, incluindo autoridades eleitorais democratas e alguns republicanos, veem o movimento como parte de um padrão de excessiva intervenção federal na supervisão de eleições. "O fato de Todd Blanche e o Departamento de Justiça estarem dispostos a apoiar isso e a colocar seus nomes nisso é uma indicação de até onde irão depois que esta eleição terminar para tentar contestar os resultados", disse o senador democrata da Califórnia Adam Schiff ao programa "Meet the Press", da NBC, neste domingo. (Reportagem de Danielle Kayeem Nova York e Karl Plume em Chicago)

item.title: Swashbuckling Liverpool seize their moment in 2-0 win over Brighton - Reuters
item.description: Swashbuckling Liverpool seize their moment in 2-0 win over Brighton Reuters

item.title: Swashbuckling Liverpool seize their moment in 2-0 win over Brighton
item.description: Andoni Iraola was pleased his Liverpool side flew out of the blocks to cruise to a 2-0 Premier League win over Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday thanks to a Pascal Gross own goal and a superb finish from striker Alexander Isak.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Andoni Iraola was pleased his Liverpool side flew out of the blocks to cruise to a 2-0 Premier League win over Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday thanks to a Pascal Gross own goal and a superb finish from striker Alexander Isak. The two sides came out with the intention of pressing high and countering quickly, and it was Liverpool who got the upper hand with two first-half goals to build a lead they never relinquished to register their first league win at home this term. "Very happy for today, very happy overall for this win ... we needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win duels, be dangerous in transitions, and I think we've done that," Iraola told reporters. Brighton's Yasin Ayari blazed an early chance over the bar and later hit the woodwork, but that was as close as the visitors came as Liverpool threw off the shackles of a shaky start to the league season to show a glimpse of what they are capable of doing. With Cody Gakpo to the left, Bradley Barcola to the right and Isak through the centre, Liverpool boast a broad, balanced attack, but they have struggled to find harmony in the opening weeks of the campaign. On Sunday that began to look like a thing of the past as Gakpo repeatedly attacked down his flank, occasionally cutting inside to keep his marker guessing and causing havoc while trying to either fashion shooting chances or pick out better-placed teammates. Liverpool's second goal came from Barcola winning the ball high up the field and squaring to Isak, whose deft first-time finish gave the keeper no chance. "Alex, I think, as a striker, if we can put him in those positions and we can provide him good crosses, good situations, he will score the goals," Iraola said. "It's a matter of, in this case Bradley, winning the duel, going one against one, being faster than the opposition and finding good spots." After an injury-plagued first season, Isak is looking more comfortable in a Liverpool shirt as he netted for the third league game in a row. "We had a lot of chances in the first half where we won the ball and countered. We could have had more goals, but yeah, Bradley done super, super good, and for me, it was just about being in the right place to finish it off," he told Sky Sports.

item.title: Audi defende plano de investimento de US$4 bi nos EUA anunciado por Trump
item.description: O presidente-executivo da montadora alemã Audi, Gernot Döllner, defendeu neste domingo o investimento planejado de US$4 bilhões em uma nova fábrica nos Estados Unidos, anunciado pelo presidente Donald Trump durante campanha para as eleições legislativas de novembro.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, David Shepardson, Rachel More
item.content:encoded: O presidente-executivo da montadora alemã Audi, Gernot Döllner, defendeu neste domingo o investimento planejado de US$4 bilhões em uma nova fábrica nos Estados Unidos, anunciado pelo presidente Donald Trump durante campanha para as eleições legislativas de novembro. Döllner esteve ao lado de Trump em um comício realizado no sábado em Perry, próximo a Macon, no centro da Geórgia, quando o presidente dos EUA afirmou que a Audi, parte do grupo Volkswagen , pretende construir uma fábrica de montagem no Estado capaz de produzir 200 mil SUVs por ano. "Essa decisão foi precedida por muitos meses de planejamento cuidadoso e intensas negociações", disse Döllner a jornalistas neste domingo. "Se o presidente dos Estados Unidos o convida, você aceita o convite. É isso que o respeito ao cargo e ao país onde investimos exige." Uma decisão final sobre o investimento ainda precisará ser aprovada pelo conselho de supervisão da Volkswagen para que o projeto avance. A Geórgia terá disputas eleitorais acirradas para o Senado dos EUA e para o governo estadual, e Trump busca demonstrar que suas tarifas sobre o setor automotivo estão ajudando a economia norte-americana e fortalecendo a manufatura no país. Na Alemanha, as tarifas ampliaram as pressões sobre a indústria europeia e aumentaram as tensões entre a direção da Volkswagen e os trabalhadores, que enfrentam cortes de empregos e possíveis fechamentos de fábricas. Segundo a Audi, as tarifas impostas por Trump sobre automóveis, aço, alumínio e peças custaram à empresa cerca de 1,2 bilhão de euros no ano passado, já que todos os veículos vendidos pela marca no mercado norte-americano são importados da Europa ou do México. Críticos das tarifas afirmam que elas também têm efeitos negativos nos Estados Unidos, elevando os preços dos veículos e atrasando alguns investimentos do setor automobilístico. Um porta-voz do sindicato alemão IG Metall afirmou que a decisão de Döllner de participar do evento com Trump durante a campanha eleitoral era "difícil de compreender". "Trump nunca deixou dúvidas sobre o que pretende: enfraquecer nossa economia doméstica, especialmente o setor automotivo", disse o porta-voz. Christiane Benner, presidente do IG Metall e vice-presidente do conselho de supervisão da Volkswagen, afirmou que é "correto e necessário" melhorar a posição da empresa no mercado norte-americano com uma nova fábrica. "No entanto, perspectivas sólidas para os trabalhadores em todas as unidades, particularmente na Alemanha, precisam ser claramente definidas e estabelecidas", afirmou. Döllner recusou-se a fornecer detalhes completos sobre o acordo de investimento com os Estados Unidos, inclusive se ele inclui algum tipo de alívio tarifário para a empresa. TRABALHADORES ALEMÃES Olaf Lies, governador do Estado alemão da Baixa Saxônia, segundo maior acionista da Volkswagen, disse que uma ampliação da produção nos Estados Unidos representa uma oportunidade, desde que os trabalhadores alemães também sejam beneficiados. "O crescimento na América deve garantir empregos e geração de valor aqui e não substituí-los", afirmou. A Audi informou que o investimento criará aproximadamente 4.500 empregos. A construção da fábrica deve começar no próximo ano, com o início da produção previsto para o começo da década de 2030. A unidade deverá montar os SUVs Audi Q7, Q8 e Q9, disse uma autoridade norte-americana à Reuters. A Audi também planeja produzir 25 mil veículos por ano no vizinho Estado da Carolina do Sul, acrescentou a autoridade. Parte desses veículos, atualmente fabricados na Europa, passaria a ser exportada a partir dos Estados Unidos. Esses veículos serão montados em uma fábrica de US$2 bilhões da marca de veículos off-road Scout Motors, do grupo Volkswagen, atualmente em construção em Blythewood, próximo à capital estadual Columbia, segundo a autoridade. "Consideramos a região um mercado fundamental para crescimento rentável", afirmou o presidente-executivo da Volkswagen, Oliver Blume. "Uma possível fábrica da Audi nos Estados Unidos criará condições adicionais para isso." Um Audi dourado com placas da fabricante estava estacionado em frente ao local do comício de Trump no sábado. (Reportagem de Bo Erickson, em Perry, e David Shepardson, em Washington; reportagem adicional de Christoph Steitz e Rachel More)

item.title: Rangers sign G James Reimer to one-year contract - Reuters
item.description: Rangers sign G James Reimer to one-year contract Reuters

item.title: Rangers sign G James Reimer to one-year contract
item.description: The New York Rangers signed goaltender James Reimer to a one-year contract on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Rangers signed goaltender James Reimer to a one-year contract on Sunday. Financial terms were not disclosed, although multiple outlets reported the deal was worth $850,000. Reimer is expected to serve as the backup to Dylan Garand, who has been New York's top goaltender since former Vezina Trophy winner Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season due to a knee injury. Reimer, 38, has played one game for Hartford of the American Hockey League this season after appearing in 14 games for the Ottawa Senators in 2025-26. He is 232-191-67 with 32 shutouts, a 2.88 goals-against average and a .909 save percentage in 539 career games (492 starts) with the Toronto Maple Leafs, San Jose Sharks, Florida Panthers, Carolina Hurricanes, Detroit Red Wings, Anaheim Ducks, Buffalo Sabres and Senators. He was selected by the Maple Leafs in the fourth round of the 2006 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Uganda reforça medidas contra Ebola e impõe quarentena de 21 dias a cidadãos que retornam do Congo
item.description: Cidadãos ugandenses que retornarem ao país após viajar para a República Democrática do Congo terão de cumprir quarentena de 21 dias, informou neste domingo o ministro da Saúde de Uganda, Chris Baryomunsi, enquanto o país reforça as medidas de prevenção contra o Ebola.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Cidadãos ugandenses que retornarem ao país após viajar para a República Democrática do Congo terão de cumprir quarentena de 21 dias, informou neste domingo o ministro da Saúde de Uganda, Chris Baryomunsi, enquanto o país reforça as medidas de prevenção contra o Ebola. Uganda afirma estar livre do Ebola após declarar o fim de seu surto mais recente em julho, mas autoridades de saúde têm demonstrado preocupação depois que duas pessoas que passaram recentemente pelo país testaram positivo posteriormente no Quênia e na Nigéria. Uganda informou que está investigando o caso registrado na Nigéria, que envolve a esposa de um diplomata suíço. A mulher, de 42 anos, retornou de Uganda para Abuja, via Adis Abeba, em 3 de outubro, segundo o Centro de Controle de Doenças da Nigéria. O órgão informou que ela permanece isolada e apresentou melhora significativa. As autoridades nigerianas rastrearam 53 contatos da paciente. Autoridades ugandenses disseram estar analisando o sequenciamento genômico, informações de viagem, interações e deslocamentos da paciente em coordenação com as autoridades da Nigéria e parceiros internacionais. Autoridades suíças haviam afirmado que se acreditava que a mulher tivesse contraído o vírus em Uganda. Baryomunsi contestou essa avaliação, dizendo que a Suíça estava "tirando conclusões prematuramente". Segundo ele, parentes da mulher oriundos da região de West Nile a visitaram em Kansanga, um subúrbio de Kampala, e esses familiares haviam viajado ao Congo. "Que evidência eles têm de que ela nunca esteve lá?", questionou. "Devemos falar de ciência, não de política." O primeiro paciente diagnosticado com Ebola no Quênia havia viajado do Congo para Uganda e embarcado em um voo do aeroporto de Entebbe para Nairóbi em 3 de outubro. O paciente morreu dois dias depois. Tanto o caso do Quênia quanto o da Nigéria passaram pelo mesmo aeroporto ugandense no mesmo dia, mas não houve qualquer interação física entre os dois pacientes, afirmou à imprensa Diana Atwine, secretária permanente do Ministério da Saúde, citando uma revisão das imagens do circuito interno de câmeras do aeroporto. Baryomunsi informou que todos os 60 contatos ligados ao caso de Ebola no Quênia concluíram o período de monitoramento de 21 dias e receberam alta do acompanhamento. "O ministério intensificou a triagem de viajantes no Aeroporto Internacional de Entebbe e em todas as passagens terrestres de fronteira. Todos os viajantes que pretendem entrar em Uganda por via aérea, terrestre ou aquática devem preencher o formulário de localização de passageiros", afirmou. Uma análise genômica do único caso confirmado de Ebola na Nigéria mostrou que o vírus é estreitamente relacionado à cepa detectada no caso índice do Quênia. Ainda assim, as autoridades nigerianas disseram não haver evidências de que o paciente do Quênia tenha viajado para a Nigéria ou mantido conexão direta com o caso registrado no país. Uganda faz fronteira com a República Democrática do Congo, onde teve início o atual surto, e já enfrentou surtos de Ebola em ocasiões anteriores. (Reportagem de Elias Biryabarema e Camillus Eboh)

item.title: Pistons C Jalen Duren (hamstring) out at least two weeks - Reuters
item.description: Pistons C Jalen Duren (hamstring) out at least two weeks Reuters

item.title: Pistons C Jalen Duren (hamstring) out at least two weeks
item.description: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be sidelined at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be sidelined at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday. Duren exited in the second quarter of Detroit's 128-111 win over the Miami Heat on Friday. Signed to a five-year, $200 million extension in the offseason, Duren is averaging 13.0 points and 7.5 rebounds in two games (both starts) this season. Duren, 22, averaged a career-best 19.5 points to go along with 10.5 rebounds per game in 2025-26. The first-time All-Star and third-team All-NBA player saw his numbers sag to 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds in 14 games of last season's playoffs. Duren has averaged 13.5 points and 10.3 rebounds in 278 career games (241 starts) since being selected by the Charlotte Hornets with the 13th overall pick of the 2022 NBA Draft. He was promptly traded to the New York Knicks on draft night before being dealt to the Pistons two weeks later. --Field Level Media
