item.title: La prix Nobel Maria Corina Machado est rentrée au Venezuela
item.description: La cheffe de file de l'opposition vénézuélienne, Maria Corina Machado, a annoncé dimanche être rentrée dans son pays après avoir passé près d'un an dans la clandestinité à l'étranger.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La cheffe de file de l'opposition vénézuélienne, Maria Corina Machado, a annoncé dimanche être rentrée dans son pays après avoir passé près d'un an dans la clandestinité à l'étranger. "Je suis là. Avec vous tous", a écrit la lauréate du prix Nobel de la paix sur les réseaux sociaux. Maria Corina Machado s'est rendue dans une église de l'Etat de Lara, dans l'ouest du pays, selon des images diffusées par son service de presse, qui a dit qu'elle se rendrait dans la capitale Caracas en voiture. Un journaliste de Reuters a vu des passants l'acclamer, chanter l'hymne national et crier "Liberté" au passage de son véhicule. Le retour de l'opposante au Venezuela risque de tendre les relations avec l'administration Trump aux États-Unis, qu'elle s'efforçait de rallier à sa cause avant même que celle-ci ne destitue le président Nicolas Maduro en janvier. Donald Trump a exprimé à plusieurs reprises son soutien à la présidente par intérim Delcy Rodriguez, ancienne adjointe de Nicolas Maduro, et s'est félicité des accords conclus sur la production pétrolière et d'autres projets commerciaux menés par des entreprises américaines dans le pays. Le président américain, qui a jugé en septembre qu'il était prématuré d'envisager des élections démocratiques au Venezuela, a déclaré dimanche qu'il ne savait pas que Maria Corina Machado était rentrée dans son pays. "J'espère qu'elle est en sécurité", a-t-il ajouté. L'opposante, qui avait fui le Venezuela fin 2025 alors qu'elle était sous le coup d'une interdiction de sortie du territoire, a déclaré que seul un "gouvernement sérieux et démocratique" pouvait apporter la stabilité dont ont besoin les investisseurs internationaux. Ce n'est pas l'avis de l'administration Trump, dont le secrétaire à l'Energie, Chris Wright, a co-présidé avec Delcy Rodriguez une cérémonie de signature de contrats énergétiques le mois dernier.

item.title: Trump has no designs on taking over state elections, US attorney general says - Reuters
item.description: Trump has no designs on taking over state elections, US attorney general says Reuters

item.title: Trump has no designs on taking over state elections, US attorney general says
item.description: The Justice Department's bid to preemptively block the results of Alaska's Senate race is not an attempt to give US President Donald Trump control of state elections, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Justice Department's bid to preemptively block the results of Alaska's Senate race is not an attempt to give US President Donald Trump control of state elections, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Sunday. Blanche's agency on Friday [USN:L1N4690RO TEXT:"sued to stop Alaska"] from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses narrowly. But the Justice Department is not setting the stage for overturning an election result if it's unfavorable to Trump, Blanche said. "President Trump is not trying to take over a state election in any way, shape, or form," Blanche told CNN's "State of the Union" program. "We're not laying any groundwork for the president to do that." Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are preparing for potential federal interference in the November 3 midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress, including legal challenges and disputes over voting that could disrupt certification of the results. In addition to the Alaska lawsuit, the Trump administration has taken other vote-related actions against states, including a lawsuit to [USN:L6N46900Y TEXT:"stop California from counting"] certain mail-in ballots and a mostly unsuccessful attempt to force 30 states and the District of Columbia to provide complete voter rolls. The Alaska action is specific to that state, Blanche said, reiterating the Trump administration's contention that voters will be "confused" because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names: incumbent US Senator Dan S. Sullivan and challenger Dan J. Sullivan Jr. The latter Sullivan is only running "to confuse voters," Blanche said. "Never before have opponents gone to such lengths to try to thwart and cheat an election as they're doing in this case," Blanche told CNN. Dan J. Sullivan has denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan. His campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit was filed to give officials "the ability to determine whether there was confusion that violates the law," Blanche said. He declined to comment on whether Trump ordered him to file the lawsuit, although the [USN:S0N46202X TEXT:"president himself"] has said he did so. Trump briefly spoke about Alaska again on Sunday, accusing Democrats of orchestrating Dan J. Sullivan's campaign. "They've made it very unclear and I think it's very unfair," Trump told reporters before boarding a flight to Michigan. "I think it's illegal because it's unfair. You want fairness in voting." But critics, including Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the move as part of a pattern of federal overreach in election oversight. "The fact that Todd Blanche and the Justice Department are willing to go along with it, they're willing to put their name on it, is an indication of how far they will go after this election is over to try to challenge the results," US Senator Adam Schiff, a California Democrat, told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday.

item.title: Sri Lanka rescues 40 Iranian sailors, spokesman says
item.description: Sri Lanka coordinated the rescue of 40 Iranian sailors from multiple commercial ships in international waters off the coast of the country and supported their return to Iran, a spokesman for the island nation's foreign ministry said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Uditha Jayasinghe
item.content:encoded: Sri Lanka coordinated the rescue of 40 Iranian sailors from multiple commercial ships in international waters off the coast of the country and supported their return to Iran, a spokesman for the island nation's foreign ministry said on Sunday. The ministry received a request from the Iranian embassy via diplomatic channels to rescue the sailors, Thushara Rodrigo, a spokesman for the ministry, said, adding they had been suffering unspecified medical emergencies. The ministry didn't give any further details of why they had to be rescued but local media including Indian national newspaper The Hindu reported they were on board vessels which were US-sanctioned oil tankers. Washington has imposed a [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"blockade"] on Iranian shipping as part of its war on Iran. The sailors from 19 ships were brought ashore at Galle Harbour, about 126 km from commercial capital Colombo, and were given medical treatment before returning to Iran early on Sunday morning, the spokesman added. Sri Lanka's navy and coastguard typically provide support during humanitarian efforts, a government source with direct knowledge of the rescue told Reuters. Earlier this year Sri Lanka rescued dozens of Iranian sailors on humanitarian grounds after the Iranian warship [USN:L1N3ZS08S TEXT:"IRIS Dena"] was sunk by a torpedo from a U.S. submarine on March 4. The bodies of more than 80 sailors who died in the attack were flown back to [USN:L1N4010BH TEXT:"Iran"] in mid-March. Thirty-two survivors of the sunken ship, as well as 208 crew members from another vessel, were returned to Iran in April.

item.title: TRE da Bahia determina prisão de secretário de Salvador sob acusação de restrição de transporte público
item.description: O presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral da Bahia (TRE-BA), Mauricio Szporer, determinou no início da tarde deste domingo a prisão do secretário municipal de Mobilidade de Salvador, Pablo Souza, sob acusação de ter orientado a redução da frota de ônibus na cidade no dia do segundo turno das eleições.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral da Bahia (TRE-BA), Mauricio Szporer, determinou no início da tarde deste domingo a prisão do secretário municipal de Mobilidade de Salvador, Pablo Souza, sob acusação de ter orientado a redução da frota de ônibus na cidade no dia do segundo turno das eleições. A decisão também fixou prazo para que fosse comprovada a circulação integral da frota, sob pena de multa de R$1 milhão por hora em caso de descumprimento. “Cumpra-se com a urgência máxima que o plantão do dia de votação exige”, disse o desembargador no documento, enfatizando que a orientação para redução da frota partiu da secretaria. Após denúncia de eleitores de que o número de veículos em circulação não correspondia à quantidade normal disponibilizada nos dias de semana, representantes do TRE estiveram neste domingo na garagem onde fica a frota de ônibus da cidade para uma inspeção, segundo a corte. "Constatou-se a presença de diversos veículos na garagem e o supervisor do local, Igor Cesar da Cruz Moraes, informou que a frota em atividade nesta data é inferior à dos dias da semana", apontou o documento. Em nota publicada nas redes sociais da prefeitura de Salvador, a secretaria disse ter determinado que todos os ônibus fossem liberados das garagens "ainda que estivessem com adesivação considerada como propaganda irregular". Em entrevista ao jornal Folha de S.Paulo, o prefeito de Salvador, Bruno Reis (União Brasil), afirmou que 75 ônibus ficaram temporariamente retidos na garagem de uma empresa pela manhã após sindicalistas supostamente terem colado adesivos do PT nas janelas dos veículos. Segundo o prefeito, após a retirada dos adesivos, os ônibus passaram a circular. O governador da Bahia, Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT), afirmou em publicação em redes sociais que colocaria policiais militares habilitados à disposição para dirigir ônibus, se necessário. “Não vou aceitar o que estão fazendo com a população baiana, tentando impedir que as pessoas exerçam seu direito ao voto”, disse. O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou em entrevista a jornalistas que a corte recebeu uma demanda para prolongar o período de votação do segundo turno e, sem dar detalhes, disse que "isso certamente, como toda e qualquer ação, será analisado a seu tempo". "De fato, em alguns locais há uma dificuldade ainda no transporte, já está sendo corrigida", disse. Ele acrescentou que o TSE está recebendo, periodicamente, relatórios do TRE da Bahia. Segundo dados do TSE, Salvador tem 1,9 milhão de eleitores aptos a votar. No primeiro turno, 1,5 milhão compareceram às urnas. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) teve 65,26% dos votos válidos na capital baiana (944.358 votos), contra 27,03% para Flávio Bolsonaro (391.188 votos). Em entrevista à imprensa na tarde de domingo, Lula disse que pediu à corte eleitoral que prorrogue o horário de votação neste domingo, citando dificuldades no transporte em Salvador, Feira de Santana e São Paulo, entre outras cidades. “Ninguém pode desistir de votar porque algum empresário sacana ou algum prefeito mau caráter, bandido, tentou evitar”, afirmou. Em São Paulo, o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral (TRE) atendeu a um pedido do PSOL e determinou que a prefeitura colocasse 100% da frota de ônibus para circular neste domingo, com multa de R$100 mil ao prefeito e ao presidente da SPTrans em caso de descumprimento. Em 2022, também houve acusações de restrição de transporte no país no dia do segundo turno, que foi marcado por operações da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), com abordagens de centenas de transportes públicos para eleitores mesmo após a proibição do TSE. Silvinei Vasques, que era diretor-geral da PRF naquele momento, chegou a ser preso.

item.title: Baylor fires football coach Dave Aranda - Reuters
item.description: Baylor fires football coach Dave Aranda Reuters

item.title: Baylor fires football coach Dave Aranda
item.description: Baylor fired head football coach Dave Aranda in his seventh season on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Baylor fired head football coach Dave Aranda in his seventh season on Sunday. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will serve as the interim coach of the Bears. He is a veteran defensive coordinator who came from Kansas State earlier this year. The moves come one day after Baylor dropped a 25-24 decision to Kansas. The Bears (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) have lost two in a row following a four-game winning streak. "Anyone who knows Dave Aranda understands what a genuine and honorable person he is and how much he deeply cares for his players, staff and this University," athletic director Doug McNamee said. "He is a gifted coach and a brilliant football mind whose leadership brought some of our best Baylor football memories. "While this is a difficult moment, we believe a change in leadership is necessary at this time for our program. We will forever be thankful to Dave and his family for their time here at Baylor, and we wish them well." Aranda, 50, is 40-40 during his time with Baylor, plus 1-2 in bowl games. He helped the Bears to a Sugar Bowl victory and a 12-2 record in 2021. His job security was called into question, however, after the club limped to 6-7 and 3-9 finishes over the next two seasons. An 8-5 finish in 2024 quieted the rumors briefly before a 5-7 record in 2025 brought about more questions. --Field Level Media

item.title: Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns home after fraught year away
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned home on Sunday after nearly a year away, and after several failed attempts to return that strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Sequera, Sarah Kinosian, Keren Torres
item.content:encoded: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned home on Sunday after nearly a year away, and after several failed attempts to return that strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration. "I'm here. With you all," the Nobel Peace Prize-winner wrote on X. She appeared at a church in western Lara state, according to images shared by her press team, and was greeted by bystanders who sang the national anthem and shouted "liberty!" as she left in an SUV, a Reuters witness said. She will travel to Caracas by road, her team said. Her efforts to return have tested her relationship with the Trump administration, which [USN:L4N3W51LU TEXT:"she has sought to cultivate as an ally"] since before it removed President Nicolas Maduro from power in January. US officials have asked her at least once to [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"delay her return"], Reuters reported in June, and she has made [USN:L1N45F02O TEXT:"several failed attempts"] to enter the country. Her team did not disclose details how she returned. Trump has repeatedly expressed support for interim President Delcy Rodriguez, former deputy to ousted President Nicolas Maduro, and hailed deals on oil production and other business ventures by US companies in the South American country. Trump said in September it was [USN:L1N44V0SA TEXT:"too soon to consider democratic elections"] in Venezuela. At the White House on Sunday, Trump said he did not know anything about Machado's return and suggested the US would continue to back Rodriguez. "She's a very nice woman," he said, referring to Machado. "But we're doing really well in Venezuela.” Machado took a private plane from Panama to Colombia and then crossed overland to Venezuela, two people with knowledge of the matter said. "The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms. Machado to Venezuela are the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks which have already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. "We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy." A faction of the opposition and the interim government held their latest session of talks this month, with the aim of remaking the top court and electoral council, among other goals, ahead of eventual elections. They do not include Machado's political movement. The Venezuelan communications ministry, which handles all press queries for the government, did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Machado's return. MEETING WITH VICTIMS "Maria Corina Machado will achieve liberty and democracy in Venezuela," said Hernan Adames, 69, as he celebrated with other supporters in Barquisimeto. Machado plans to meet with victims of the deadly earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, as well as the families of political prisoners, the international community and various leaders from the democratic movement in Venezuela, David Smolansky, her top foreign affairs adviser, told Reuters. "She will work proactively for a date for free and fair elections," he added. International energy firms committed last month to [USN:L1N44U0I0 TEXT:"expanding projects"] in the country in a signing ceremony overseen by Rodriguez and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright. Machado has said that only a "serious, democratic government" can provide the stability needed by investors. She had been barred by Maduro's government from exiting Venezuela but she secretly left in late 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, after spending more than a year living mostly in hiding. Machado's Vente Venezuela movement [USN:L6N4611CS TEXT:"debuted an app on Saturday"] to collect voter registration information from Venezuelans abroad. The group hopes eventually to share data from the app, which was built by 15 staff over the last 18 months, with a reformed electoral council so users can be officially added to voter rolls. Edmundo Gonzalez, a former presidential candidate for Machado's movement who has been living in Spain, said on X he would soon join her in Venezuela.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers topple Saints in Paris
item.description: Aaron Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown passes list, Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and the Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 on Sunday in the first NFL game played in Paris.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Aaron Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown passes list, Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and the Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 on Sunday in the first NFL game played in Paris. For the second straight year, Rodgers was responsible for the NFL's first touchdown throw in a foreign country. In 2025, he delivered the league's first-ever TD pass in Ireland. The Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game after shutting out the Saints (2-5) in the second half in Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of Paris. Tyler Shough passed for 278 yards with a touchdown and an interception for New Orleans, which rushed for just 18 yards -- 130 fewer than Pittsburgh. The Saints received the second-half kickoff and drove into position for a tying field goal or go-ahead touchdown by reaching the Steelers' 10, but Shough was intercepted by Payton Wilson. On the ensuing possession, Rodgers drove Pittsburgh to a first down at the New Orleans 14 before the march stalled. Chris Boswell kicked a 39-yard field to increase the Steelers' lead to 16-10 at the end of the third quarter. The Saints moved into field-goal range before Daniel Carlson's 52-yard attempt sailed wide right. Rodgers' 8-yard scramble on a third-and-6 from the New Orleans 34 helped Pittsburgh run out the clock. The Steelers drove to Boswell's 28-yard field goal on the first possession of the game, and the 3-0 lead held through the end of the first quarter. Carlson's 38-yard field goal tied the score early in the second quarter. Rodgers' 51-yard completion to DK Metcalf set up his 4-yard touchdown pass to tight end Darnell Washington to give Pittsburgh a 10-3 lead. That was Rodgers' 540th career touchdown pass, breaking a tie with Manning for third place on the NFL's all-time list. Barion Brown returned the ensuing kickoff 42 yards to the New Orleans 48. Shough completed all seven of his passes on the possession, the last being a 1-yard touchdown to Devaughn Vele to tie the score at 10. Boswell's 47-yard field goal as time expired gave the Steelers a 13-10 halftime lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Liverpool grab home win, Man United slump to another defeat as pressure mounts on Carrick
item.description: Michael Carrick left Bruno Fernandes out of United's starting team after criticizing the coach's tactics.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool beat Brighton & Hove Albion 2-0 on Sunday to grab their first home win of the Premier League season while Manchester United slumped to an embarrassing 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth that will heap further pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick, who benched captain Bruno Fernandes. The Portuguese playmaker was left out of the starting team after criticising Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 Champions League defeat to Italian side Como in midweek. Any hope that the move might inspire the rest of the side evaporated when Rayan scored for the Cherries in the 38th minute, with Marcus Tavernier adding a second goal before the break. Evanilson's superb third had a trickle of fans head for the exits, and that trickle became a flood as the end approached with Fernandes still on the bench and very little sign that United would be capable of mounting any sort of comeback. With the final whistle greeted by a loud chorus of boos, the defeat left Carrick's side in 16th place on seven points, one above the relegation zone, and they are without a win in the league since beating Ipswich Town 5-2 on August 30. WHAT NEXT FOR CARRICK? The only consolation for the beleaguered coach came from the fans who remained to cheer him as he left the pitch before booing the players who had again failed to deliver on the field. "It wasn't a farewell from me. I'm mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it, the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment," he told Sky Sports before admitting that his future was uncertain. "It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won't change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see." Stand-in captain Harry Maguire said that the United players needed to take a long, hard look in the mirror. "That's the most important thing - think what you can do more and what more you can contribute to the team, and if we do that we'll get somewhere," he told Sky Sports. "This is a huge club and every day you have to prove why you're wearing this badge. At the moment, we're not doing enough as players. Michael turned our season on its head last year, and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results - this season, we haven't performed well enough as individuals." SEAGULLS GROUNDED BY LIVERPOOL Liverpool enjoyed a much more positive afternoon as they welcomed high-flying Brighton to Anfield, netting twice in a high-energy first half to bring an excellent run of four league wins on the trot for the Seagulls to a shuddering halt. Brighton defender Pascal Gross steered a Florian Wirtz shot into his own net in the 17th minute, and Alexander Isak scored the second with a deftly taken first-time finish from Bradley Barcola's pass four minutes later to secure the win. "I think today the performance was really good, really solid, against a really good team," Isak said after netting for the third league game in a row. "The first half is really what we want to be about - intensity and winning balls and countering. So yeah, I'm really happy, especially with the first half." The win lifts Liverpool to fourth in the table on 15 points, one behind Brighton. Manchester City remain top of the standings on 21 points despite dropping their first points of the season on Saturday in a 2-1 reverse against Aston Villa, with Arsenal in second place on goal difference. Newcastle United got back to winning ways with a 2-0 win away to Crystal Palace, while Hull City were held to a 1-1 draw at home to Brentford. Sunderland against Leeds United ended in a scoreless stalemate.

item.title: Final round in Bermuda scrapped; 2-man playoff set for Monday morning
item.description: The Butterfield Bermuda Championship is headed for a Monday playoff between Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman after play was scrapped Sunday due to inclement weather and the PGA Tour shortened regulation to 54 holes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Butterfield Bermuda Championship is headed for a Monday playoff between Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman after play was scrapped Sunday due to inclement weather and the PGA Tour shortened regulation to 54 holes. Golfers waited for word from the tour after it was decided early on Sunday that the entire fourth round would be postponed due to heavy rain and high winds. The next update came at 5:17 p.m. local time at Port Royal Golf Course in Southampton. "Due to the unfavorable weather forecast for Monday at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship and the uncertainty surrounding the completion of the entire final round on Monday, the tournament results will be considered final through 54 holes in accordance with PGA Tour regulations," the tour said in a statement. The playoff between Smotherman and the Irishman Power is tentatively scheduled for 9 a.m. local time Monday. They will compete in a sudden-death playoff to determine the winner. Smotherman, who captured his first PGA Tour title earlier this month at the Bank of Utah Championship, and Power were tied at 16-under-par 197 after three rounds. Wind gusts topped 40 mph on Sunday morning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Líder da oposição venezuelana Corina Machado retorna à Venezuela
item.description: A líder da oposição venezuelana Maria Corina Machado retornou à Venezuela após passar quase um ano fora do país, anunciou ela própria em uma publicação nas redes sociais neste domingo.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Kinosian, Vivian Sequera
item.content:encoded: A líder da oposição venezuelana Maria Corina Machado retornou à Venezuela após passar quase um ano fora do país, anunciou ela própria em uma publicação nas redes sociais neste domingo. "Estou aqui. Com todos vocês", escreveu Machado, vencedora do Prêmio Nobel da Paz, em uma mensagem publicada nas primeiras horas deste domingo. A equipe de imprensa de Machado divulgou imagens dela no Estado de Lara, no centro-oeste do país, na Plaza del Pueblo de Santa Rosa, onde a líder opositora apareceu em uma igreja. A questão de seu retorno tem gerado tensões em sua relação com o governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que ela vinha tentando cultivar como aliado desde antes da saída do poder do presidente Nicolás Maduro, em janeiro. Trump tem manifestado repetidamente apoio à presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez, ex-vice de Maduro, e elogiado acordos de produção de petróleo e outros empreendimentos de empresas norte-americanas na Venezuela. Em setembro, Trump afirmou que ainda era cedo para considerar a realização de eleições democráticas no país. Falando na Casa Branca neste domingo, Trump disse não ter conhecimento do retorno de Machado à Venezuela e indicou que os Estados Unidos continuariam apoiando Rodríguez. "Ela é uma mulher muito simpática", afirmou, referindo-se a Machado. "Mas estamos indo muito bem na Venezuela." Em entrevista à Fox News neste domingo, Trump também afirmou que os Estados Unidos tinham "controle total sobre a Venezuela". "Estamos sendo muito justos", disse. "Mas estamos retirando milhões de barris de petróleo por semana." Nem a Casa Branca nem o Ministério da Comunicação da Venezuela, responsável por responder às consultas da imprensa em nome do governo, responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário sobre o retorno de Machado. Machado pretende se reunir com vítimas dos terremotos mortais que atingiram a Venezuela em junho, bem como com familiares de presos políticos, representantes da comunidade internacional e diversos líderes do movimento democrático venezuelano, disse à Reuters David Smolansky, seu principal assessor para assuntos internacionais. "Ela trabalhará ativamente para definir uma data para eleições livres e justas", acrescentou. Empresas internacionais do setor de energia comprometeram-se no mês passado a ampliar seus projetos no país durante uma cerimônia acompanhada por Rodríguez e pelo secretário de Energia dos EUA, Chris Wright. Machado tem afirmado que apenas um "governo sério e democrático" pode oferecer a estabilidade necessária aos investidores. Em junho, ela declarou que faria o que fosse necessário para voltar ao país e ajudar os sobreviventes dos dois terremotos devastadores daquele mês, que mataram pelo menos 6.500 pessoas e deixaram milhares de desaparecidos. Machado estava impedida pelo governo Maduro de deixar a Venezuela, mas saiu secretamente do país no fim de 2025 para receber o Prêmio Nobel da Paz, após passar mais de um ano vivendo majoritariamente na clandestinidade. Seu desejo de retornar provocou atritos em Washington, com autoridades norte-americanas pedindo que ela adiasse a viagem, informou a Reuters em junho. Machado não revelou mais detalhes sobre seu paradeiro atual nem sobre como retornou ao país. Uma facção da oposição e o governo interino realizaram neste mês sua mais recente rodada de negociações, que busca reformular o Tribunal Supremo de Justiça e o Conselho Nacional Eleitoral, entre outros objetivos, com vistas a futuras eleições. O movimento político de Machado não participa dessas conversas. Edmundo González, ex-candidato presidencial do movimento de Machado e que vive na Espanha, confirmou o retorno da líder opositora em uma publicação própria e afirmou que em breve se juntará a ela. (Reportagem de Vivian Sequera e Sarah Kinosian, em Caracas)

item.title: Machado sorprende con llegada a Venezuela, seguidores celebran su vuelta
item.description: La líder opositora y Premio Nobel de la Paz María Corina Machado sorprendió el domingo al aparecer en Venezuela, tras casi un año en el extranjero, algo largamente esperado por sus seguidores, que celebraron su llegada, en lo que podría reconfigurar el futuro político del país.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Sequera, Sarah Kinosian
item.content:encoded: La líder opositora y Premio Nobel de la Paz María Corina Machado sorprendió el domingo al aparecer en Venezuela, tras casi un año en el extranjero, algo largamente esperado por sus seguidores, que celebraron su llegada, en lo que podría reconfigurar el futuro político del país. "Estoy aquí. Con ustedes", dijo Machado en su cuenta de X, sin dar más precisiones. El primer contacto de Machado con sus compatriotas fue en la Plaza del Pueblo de Santa Rosa, en el estado occidental de Lara, de acuerdo a su equipo de prensa. Machado, de camiseta blanca, apareció sorpresivamente en una iglesia de Barqusimeto, la capital de Lara, para asombro de los feligreses, mostraron imágenes divulgadas por su equipo. Más tarde, partió en un vehículo tipo SUV mientras los presentes cantaban el himno nacional y gritaban "¡libertad!", según un testigo de Reuters. Machado, de 59 años, llegó desde Panamá en un avión privado y, el domingo, cruzó por tierra desde Colombia, según informaron cuatro fuentes a Reuters. Una de las fuentes, al tanto de los movimientos y planes de Machado, señaló que su regreso fue coordinado con los gobiernos de Estados Unidos, Panamá y Colombia. El presidente Donald Trump aprobó su retorno y se mantuvo al tanto de la situación. Durante el trayecto, Machado estuvo bajo la protección de contratistas de seguridad estadounidenses, indicó la fuente. Estados Unidos advirtió a la presidente encargada venezolana Delcy Rodríguez y a las autoridades venezolanas de que no interfieran ni pongan en peligro su seguridad, añadió la fuente. La Casa Blanca y el Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos no respondieron a preguntas de Reuters. "Las condiciones que han permitido el regreso seguro de la señora Machado a Venezuela son el resultado directo de las conversaciones de reconciliación respaldadas por Estados Unidos", dijo el secretario de Estado Marco Rubio en un comunicado. "Esperamos que todos los actores políticos apoyen estas conversaciones, que representan la mejor oportunidad que ha tenido Venezuela en 30 años para lograr, de manera pacífica, no solo unas elecciones libres y justas, sino también una democracia duradera", agregó. RUMBO A CARACAS En su caravana a Caracas por carretera, en un recorrido que la llevó por varios estados, miles de personas le gritaban: "María te amamos" , "bienvenida", "libertad" y "elecciones ya", mientras la principal autopista que conecta la capital venezolana con el centro del país y por donde transitaba estaba bloqueada por la muchedumbre en el sentido hacia la principal ciudad venezolana. Machado divulgó fotos y videos de decenas de personas saludándola en la carretera mientras ella avanzaba en una camioneta blanca y se detenía en varios tramos para saludar. En Santa Mónica, una zona del oeste de caracas, Mercedes Márquez, una docente jubilada de 54 años, dijo que “lo que queremos es fecha de elecciones y que María Corina sea la candidata. Queremos cambios y que esta gente que nos ha destruida la vida 25 años se vaya". "No hemos visto, los ciudadanos, ningún cambio desde 3 de enero. Todo parece igual o peor", agregó Márquez al referirse a la fecha en que Estados Unidos capturó en una operativo militar en Caracas al presidente Nicolás Maduro. El Gobierno del depuesto presidente Nicolás Maduro le prohibió a Machado salir de Venezuela, pero ella partió en secreto a finales de 2025 para recibir el Nobel de la Paz, después de pasar más de un año viviendo en la clandestinidad. Más temprano, el presidente Trump, al ser consultado sobre el regreso de Machado, dijo que "no sé nada al respecto. Pero creo que es una mujer muy agradable. Me entregó su Premio Nobel, así que ¿cómo podría decir otra cosa? Y espero que esté a salvo. Es una mujer muy agradable, pero nos está yendo muy bien en Venezuela". La cuestión de su regreso ha tensado su relación con Washington, y Trump ha señalado en varias oportunidades que la presidenta encargada Rodríguez, es "fantástica". El Ministerio de Comunicación de Venezuela, que gestiona todas las consultas de la prensa dirigidas al Gobierno, no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. En agosto, una facción de la oposición y el Gobierno encargado, bajo el apoyo de Estados Unidos, iniciaron conversaciones en busca de reformar el sistema político del país antes de las elecciones, en un proceso en el que no está participando Vente Venezuela, el movimiento de Machado. Machado planea reunirse con las víctimas de los terremotos que azotaron Venezuela en junio, así como con las familias de los prisioneros políticos, dijo a Reuters David Smolansky, su principal asesor de asuntos exteriores. "Ella trabajará de manera proactiva para fijar una fecha para elecciones libres y justas", añadió. El movimiento opositor de Machado se prepara para unas eventuales elecciones, lo que incluye una nueva iniciativa para impulsar el registro de votantes, según documentos y fuentes conocedoras del asunto.

item.title: AstraZeneca's stomach cancer drug extends overall survival, late-stage trial data finds
item.description: AstraZeneca's experimental drug sone-ve helped patients with advanced stomach cancer who had received at least two prior treatments to live longer than analysts had expected, according to late-stage trial data presented on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija
item.content:encoded: AstraZeneca's (AZN.L) experimental drug sone-ve helped patients with advanced stomach cancer who had received at least two prior treatments to live longer than analysts had expected, according to late-stage trial data presented on Sunday. Patients on the drug lived a median of 10 months, compared with 5 months on their doctor's choice of chemotherapy, a 53% reduction in the risk of death. "A 5-month improvement in overall survival is very clinically significant in a difficult to treat patient population," said Susan Galbraith, executive vice president of oncology haematology research and development at AstraZeneca. A win on overall survival could boost confidence in the drug's commercial potential, as it did not reach statistical significance on its other goal of progression-free survival in the study. AstraZeneca has said it expects the drug could bring in between $3 billion and $5 billion in peak sales, but analysts' estimates are closer to $1 billion. The drug, sonesitatug vedotin, or sone-ve, belongs to a class of treatments called antibody drug conjugates, or ADCs, often described as guided missiles as they deliver therapy to cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. "It's another data set that reinforces our vision that we've had for a long time, that ADCs can replace and improve on backbone chemotherapy in many different tumour types," Galbraith said. Analysts were expecting an overall survival hazard ratio, or risk of death, of about 0.7 or lower, with a gain of at least 2 months. ASTRAZENECA INVESTS IN AND WORKS WITH SUMMIT THERAPEUTICS The detailed data from the 532-patient study was presented at the conference of the European Society for Medical Oncology in Madrid on Sunday, a month after AstraZeneca agreed to invest $2 billion in the biopharmaceutical company Summit Therapeutics and to test sone-ve alongside Summit's bispecific antibody ivonescimab. Patients with gastroesophageal cancer in AstraZeneca's study were enrolled if at least 25% of their tumour cells showed claudin 18.2, a protein found on many cancer cells. The approved treatment for this target requires a 75% cutoff. Galbraith said the lower threshold could double the number of patients who would be able to receive treatment. "I think that bodes well for the opportunity to move it into the earlier line setting," she said. Another study of more than 2,000 patients is already testing the drug earlier in a patient's course of therapy. HSBC analysts said the miss makes it harder to compare the drug with IBI343, a rival claudin 18.2 therapy being developed by Takeda (4502.T) and Innovent (1801.HK) , which succeeded on its progression-free survival goal in a late-stage study. Serious side effects were less common with AstraZeneca's drug, 36.4% versus 44.8% on chemotherapy, though stomach-related side effects were more frequent, at 11.1% versus 6.3%.

item.title: Les Brésiliens aux urnes pour un second tour serré entre Lula et Bolsonaro
item.description: Les Brésiliens votaient dimanche pour un second tour de la présidentielle qui s'annonce serré et qui pourrait faire basculer le plus grand pays d'Amérique latine vers la droite, comme nombre de pays de la région.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: Les Brésiliens votaient dimanche pour un second tour de la présidentielle qui s'annonce serré et qui pourrait faire basculer le plus grand pays d'Amérique latine vers la droite, comme nombre de pays de la région. Le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro, actuellement emprisonné, part légèrement favori face au chef de l'Etat sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, après avoir créé la surprise au début du mois en arrivant en tête au premier tour avec 47% des voix, contre 45% à Lula. Un juge de la Cour suprême a décidé de prolonger de deux heures les opérations de vote, qui devaient se terminer à 17h00 (20h00 GMT), en raison de problèmes de transports publics dénoncés par l'équipe de campagne de Lula. Une victoire de Flavio Bolsonaro, 45 ans, prolongerait la série de victoires enregistrées dans les urnes par des candidats de droite latino-américains revendiquant une proximité avec le président des États-Unis, Donald Trump. A l'inverse, un quatrième mandat de Lula ne serait pas vu d'un bon oeil par Washington, qui s'est heurté au président de gauche sur les questions commerciales et de sécurité. Samedi, Reuters a révélé l'existence d'une campagne menée par le département d'État américain pour aider les Bolsonaro à revenir au pouvoir. La campagne électorale a été marquée par des scandales de corruption et des accusations d'ingérence américaine, malgré les dénégations de Washington, avec en toile de fond la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 pour avoir fomenté un coup d'État après sa défaite à la présidentielle trois ans plus tôt, son fils s'étant engagé à le faire sortir de prison s'il est élu. Donald Trump a qualifié la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro de "chasse aux sorcières" et a imposé en représailles des droits de douane de 50% au Brésil. Bien que cette mesure ait ensuite été assouplie, les États-Unis ont imposé cette année de nouvelles sanctions au Brésil, invoquant des pratiques commerciales déloyales. ACCUSATIONS D'INGÉRENCE AMÉRICAINE Lula a accusé l'administration Trump d'ingérence électorale et dénoncé des actes d'intimidation de la part de Washington. "On ne peut pas leur livrer le Brésil", a approuvé Elenildes dos Reis, une avocate de 60 ans, après avoir voté dimanche pour Lula à São Paulo. "Ce ne sera pas seulement notre victoire, ce sera celle du monde entier", a-t-elle ajouté. Sur le plan économique, malgré la baisse des inégalités et du chômage, Lula a eu du mal à convaincre un électorat confronté à la hausse du coût de la vie et de l'endettement des ménages. Flavio Bolsonaro a promis de lutter contre la vie chère et d'adopter des méthodes musclées contre la violence des gangs qui a aussi pesé dans la campagne. "Nous avons besoin de changement", a déclaré José Carlos Jarra, un retraité de 61 ans qui a voté pour le candidat Flavio Bolsonaro à São Paulo. À Rio de Janeiro, Alba Marques, une retraitée de 75 ans, a dit avoir voté pour Flavio Bolsonaro pour sanctionner le Parti des travailleurs de Lula, et non par adhésion au programme du candidat d'extrême droite. "Je ne supporte plus qu'un type passe 40 ans à dire qu'il va redresser le Brésil. Toujours la même promesse", a-t-elle dit à propos du président octogénaire. Les derniers sondages d'intention de vote plaçaient les deux candidats au coude-à-coude à la veille du scrutin, la principale incertitude venant de la mobilisation des abstentionnistes. Aucun candidat arrivé en tête au premier tour n'a jamais perdu au second tour de la présidentielle au Brésil.

item.title: Paris game played in festive atmosphere after fresh demonstrations
item.description: Protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the first NFL regular-season game.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Daheron
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the first NFL regular-season game in Paris on Sunday, in a calm and festive atmosphere, a day after fresh demonstrations drew more than 100,000 people into the French capital. The nationwide protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the game, with some fan and NFL [USN:L6N46912R TEXT:"events cancelled"] over the weekend, mainly due to their location in central Paris. On Sunday, as Saturday’s rain gave way to sunshine, the mood was peaceful before kickoff around the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, some 10km (6 miles) north of Paris centre and more than 13km (8 miles) from Porte d'Italie, where Saturday's protests began in southern Paris. James Brown, a 51-year-old Saints fan who travelled to Paris especially for the game, told Reuters the atmosphere around the stadium was "wonderful, really good". The police presence appeared neither heavy nor unusual at the Stade de France, which hosted rugby sevens and athletics during the 2024 Paris Olympics and regularly serves as the home ground for the French national rugby and soccer teams. Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched in France on Saturday, with largely peaceful rallies giving way to clashes in Paris and Marseille as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of last week's unrest. The main demonstration took place on the southeastern fringes of Paris, where at least 110,000 people turned out to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality. "We didn't notice much yesterday," 38-year-old Steelers fan Lukas Baldridge told Reuters. "We came in, went to a bar, got some drinks, got dinner, went home, didn't see any protesting. "Streets were closed. Most shops were closed. That felt unusual maybe but I don't know enough about Paris to know what is normal and what's not normal." The party was in full swing in a packed stadium when the game kicked off at 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT), after French stars Antoine Dupont and Teddy Riner were introduced to the crowd. A couple of hours earlier, some Steelers players had arrived at the Stade de France dressed like characters from Peaky Blinders. Steelers fans seemed to outnumber their opponents, even though the neutral-site game was officially hosted by the Saints. "It kind of felt 50/50," Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss told a press conference. "This is such a fun atmosphere. Maybe not feel like the true home team, it was a very special atmosphere, one I wish we could have gotten a win in." Nigerian rapper Burna Boy and French singer Yseult performed during a brief halftime show. "I would like to start by saying how much we appreciate everyone who, in the country of France, Paris, Versailles, helped make this event happen," Saints coach Kellen Moore told a press conference. "I thought it was a really great event, really great game today."

item.title: What are Brazilian voters' main concerns?
item.description: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles
item.content:encoded: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Here are the main themes that have driven the campaign: INFLATION Cost-of-living concerns are widespread. More than two-thirds of respondents told a Quaest poll in August their purchasing power [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"had declined"] versus the previous year. Annual inflation stood at 4.58% in the 12 months through September, above the central bank's 3% target, pushing prices — including for food — higher Lula has pledged to implement measures to allow for steady cuts in borrowing costs and keep inflation under control Bolsonaro wants to reduce and stabilize public debt to bring interest rates closer to international levels and steer inflation toward the central bank's target CRIME Crime is another major [USN:L1N45Z0NR TEXT:"concern"] for Brazilians. While Brazil's homicide rate fell by 40% over the last decade, improvements in fighting crime have been uneven, according to the Brazilian Public Security Forum, a think tank. Bolsonaro has pledged a heavy-handed approach to criminals, promising maximum-security prisons and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses Lula wants to increase the federal prison system's capacity to hold gang leaders, while still investing in poor areas to reduce the influence of organized crime CORRUPTION Corruption is also at the top of voters' minds, with both Lula's circle and Bolsonaro [USN:L6N46611M TEXT:"facing scrutiny"] in high-profile cases. A major scandal that led to the collapse of mid-size lender Banco Master has sparked multiple probes, including into [USN:L6N3ZZ1EP TEXT:"Bolsonaro"] over alleged corruption and money laundering, accusations he denies Bolsonaro has pledged to fight corruption by shielding state-run companies and pension funds from political appointments and expanding transparency in public spending Lula has vowed to deepen anti-corruption and transparency policies even as his son - who has denied the allegations - is being investigated in probes involving alleged influence peddling, corruption and fraud PUBLIC FINANCES Brazil's public finances are under pressure, especially due to pensions and social benefits. The difficult fiscal outlook has sparked fears of welfare cuts, while many Brazilians are struggling with debt arrears due to years of double-digit interest rates. Public debt has risen by more than 10 percentage points during Lula's current term, reaching [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"82.9%"] of gross domestic product Brazil's benchmark interest rate of [USN:L6N458186 TEXT:"13.75%"] remains among the highest in the world Long-term interest rates [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"fell sharply"] after Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected first-round performance He has promised to ramp up [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"fiscal adjustment"], targeting 1.5% of GDP improvement in the primary balance within 18 months to lower borrowing costs Lula has reiterated commitments to improve Brazil's primary balance targeting an [USN:L1N44S10B TEXT:"effective surplus"] near 1.3% of GDP by 2030, versus a projected 0.4% deficit this year FOREIGN POLICY After US President Donald Trump imposed [USN:L6N3TR0ZD TEXT:"tariffs"] on a swathe of Brazilian goods in 2025, foreign policy became a more prominent issue for many Brazilians. Bolsonaro has courted Trump and other right-wing allies globally He wants to rebuild ties with Argentina, the US and Israel, arguing relations with each are close to breaking point Lula has campaigned for a foreign policy based on multilateralism and stronger ties with the Mercosur bloc of South American states and the BRICS nations ($1 = 5.0086 reais)

item.title: French protest groups demand more rallies as Macron faces tough choices
item.description: The government began talks with unions and student representatives to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed are inadequate.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Juliette Jabkhiro
item.content:encoded: French protest groups and unions called on Sunday for further demonstrations as they sought to maintain pressure on the government after a huge security operation helped to contain unrest during nationwide rallies on Saturday. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part in Saturday's marches as authorities deployed 70,000 police, helping to avert a repeat of the looting and vandalism that swept many cities on October 17. Labour leaders urged further protests next Saturday and a nationwide strike on November 5, saying frustration over wages, living costs and public services was spreading far beyond the student movement that first mobilised last month. "We see an aggregation of anger," Murielle Guilbert, co-leader of the left-wing Solidaires trade union federation, told BFM TV. She said grievances from students, workers, firefighters and other groups were converging. "We call on people to take to the streets next Saturday." The SUD Education teaching union said it would join the October 31 demonstration while the large CGT union said it would decide during the week. MACRON'S SCOPE TO RESPOND IS MINIMAL The Yellow Vests, a grassroots movement that emerged in 2018 as a revolt against fuel taxes, also called for mass rallies next Saturday, including sit-ins outside town halls and the National Assembly. "There is anger in this country. It's growing in schools and universities, on roundabouts, in neighbourhoods, on farms and in workplaces," activist Azelma Sigaux told reporters. In 2019, President Emmanuel Macron was able to find the resources to reduce fuel costs in response to the Yellow Vests. Seven years on, strained public finances leave him with little room to meet protesters' demands. His mandate also expires next April and his centrist party no longer has the majority needed to pass major legislation. The government has begun talks with unions and student representatives to try to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed so far are inadequate. "We have received no response at all from this government," said Guilbert. Police unions said on Sunday they did not have enough staff to maintain for any length of time the high level of deployment that on Saturday helped to limit disorder to sporadic clashes in a number of cities, including Paris and Marseille. Some 1,314 people were arrested on Saturday, half of last week's numbers, the interior ministry said on Sunday, and about 50 police were injured, compared with more than 1,000 last week. The protests have resonated beyond France's borders. On Saturday [USN:L6N46A05C TEXT:"Belgian police"] used tear gas and pepper spray as they clashed in Brussels with anti-government demonstrators. [USN:FWN4630JL TEXT:"In Albania"], peaceful protests that began at the end of May this month turned into violent unrest and skirmishes have taken place in several Italian cities for a second week running.

item.title: Brasil extiende votación en reñido balotaje presidencial entre Lula y Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región. El balotaje enfrenta al presidente izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva con el senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro. El hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro dio la sorpresa a principios de mes al liderar la votación en la primera vuelta en contra de lo que decían las encuestas. El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal Cristiano Zanin ordenó que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña de Lula. En un principio, estaba previsto que las urnas cerraran a las 17:00 hora de Brasilia (2000 GMT). La campaña de Lula denunció que las autoridades de varias ciudades estaban restringiendo el acceso de los votantes al transporte público. En tanto, la autoridad electoral del país anunció que pausaba el recuento de los sufragios hasta que se cumpla el horario ampliado de la votación. Bolsonaro solicitó tiempo adicional en tres estados, alegando mal clima, mientras que Lula pidió que ampliaran el horario de votación en nueve estados después de que su campaña denunciara que las autoridades habían reducido el servicio de transporte público el día de las elecciones. Muchos brasileños dependen del transporte público para votar en las ciudades en las que están empadronados, pero en las que quizá no residan. Los seguidores de Lula suelen depender en mayor medida del transporte público en estas ciudades. Un tribunal del estado de Bahía, bastión de Lula en el noreste, ordenó la detención de un alto cargo del transporte en Salvador por las acusaciones de que ordenó una reducción de la flota de autobuses de la ciudad. "Nadie debería renunciar a votar porque algún empresario sin escrúpulos o algún alcalde corrupto y deshonesto haya intentado impedírselo", declaró Lula a periodistas. Un triunfo de Bolsonaro, de 45 años, prolongaría la ola de victorias de la derecha para los candidatos latinoamericanos afines a Donald Trump, mientras que un cuarto mandato para Lula sería una decepción en Washington, que ha tenido roces con su gobierno en materia de comercio y seguridad. Reuters reveló el sábado una campaña dentro del Departamento de Estado de Trump para ayudar a que los Bolsonaro volvieran al poder. La contienda electoral ha estado marcada por escándalos de corrupción, incertidumbre económica y acusaciones de injerencia estadounidense, algo que Washington niega. También se ha visto influenciada por las repercusiones de la condena de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 por planear un golpe de Estado en 2022, ante la promesa de Flávio de liberar a su padre si resulta elegido. Trump calificó el caso de "caza de brujas" e impuso un arancel del 50% a Brasil en 2025, en una decisión vinculada explícitamente al juicio de Jair Bolsonaro. Si bien muchas de estas medidas fueron posteriormente suavizadas, el mandatario republicano impuso nuevos aranceles a Brasil este año, alegando prácticas comerciales desleales. Lula ha presentado la cercanía del Gobierno de Trump con el clan Bolsonaro como parte de un intento de influir en las elecciones, al tiempo que ha calificado los aranceles y otras medidas punitivas de intimidación. "No podemos entregar Brasil", afirmó Elenildes dos Reis, una abogada de 60 años de São Paulo que votó por Lula y señaló que su victoria sería una forma de plantarle cara a Trump y a lo que ella describió como una ola creciente de fascismo. "No será solo nuestra victoria, será la del mundo", añadió. En materia económica, a pesar de la disminución de la desigualdad y el desempleo, Lula ha tenido dificultades para ganarse a un electorado que lidia con el alto costo de la vida y las elevadas deudas familiares. La violencia endémica de las pandillas también preocupa a los votantes. RESULTADO INCIERTO Bolsonaro ha intentado sacar provecho de la preocupación por el costo de la vida y también ha prometido mano dura para combatir la delincuencia, comprometiéndose a construir cárceles de máxima seguridad y a aplicar la castración química para los delitos sexuales graves. "Necesitamos un cambio", afirmó José Carlos Jarra, un jubilado de 61 años de São Paulo que trabajó en el sector sanitario y votó a Bolsonaro. Dijo esperar que el senador abordara la seguridad pública y hiciera más por los jubilados, y calificó el salario mínimo de Brasil como "una vergüenza". En Río de Janeiro, Alba Marques, una jubilada de 75 años, afirmó que su voto por Bolsonaro era un voto en contra del Partido de los Trabajadores de Lula, no a favor del senador. "Ya no soporto que, desde hace 40 años, un tipo diga que va a arreglar Brasil. Siempre la misma promesa", afirmó. Al emitir su voto en Río de Janeiro el domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro instó a la gente a acudir a las urnas "con lluvia o con sol". Lula, por su parte, votará en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo. Las encuestas muestran que los candidatos están prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta, con recortando distancias en los últimos días. Lula votó en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo, y agradeció a sus seguidores. "Lo que la gente ha hecho por mí estos últimos días es algo que nunca podré devolver", dijo a periodistas. Los precedentes históricos favorecen a Bolsonaro, ya que ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia tras quedar segundo en la primera vuelta de las elecciones. Bolsonaro obtuvo el 47% de los votos emitidos en la primera vuelta, contra e 45% de Lula. La victoria del senador disparó los mercados brasileños y su moneda ante las expectativas de reformas favorables a las empresas. Su éxito en la primera vuelta se vio reflejado en las elecciones al Congreso de su Partido Liberal y de otros políticos de derecha, lo que podría allanarle el camino legislativo o complicarle la gobernabilidad a Lula.

item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas. Neste cenário, algumas cidades do país enfrentavam problemas no transporte público, e a Justiça eleitoral determinou a [USN:L2N46B04J TEXT:"prisão"] de um secretário municipal de Salvador sob acusação de restrição de transporte público. Flávio Bolsonaro, senador de 45 anos e filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, largou na frente na disputa pelo Planalto após um resultado surpreendente no primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, quando terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos, contra 45,16% de Lula. O atual presidente e candidato à reeleição, que completará 81 anos na próxima terça-feira e que busca um quarto mandato presidencial, reduziu gradativamente a distância para o rival nas pesquisas de intenção de voto mais recentes, o que leva a corrida a um cenário incerto. “O que o povo fez comigo nesses dias é uma coisa que não tem como pagar, é muita generosidade, é muito carinho, é muito amor e eu serei eternamente grato ao comportamento do povo”, disse o petista a jornalistas após votar na manhã deste domingo, em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), berço político do Partido dos Trabalhadores. As [USN:L2N46A047 TEXT:"pesquisas divulgadas na véspera"] da votação deste domingo mostraram um empate técnico com vantagem numérica de Flávio sobre Lula de no máximo dois pontos percentuais nos votos válidos, com 51% a 49%. "Flávio é ligeiramente favorito, ele não é francamente favorito", disse o cientista político Carlos Melo, do Insper. "Quando você olha para as pesquisas, mais do que o número você tem que olhar para a tendência. A tendência é o Flávio caindo, ou praticamente paralisado, e o Lula subindo muito devagar", acrescentou, apontando que não é possível prever se essa tendência resultará em uma virada a favor de Lula neste domingo. Um dos fatores cruciais a ser observado, na avaliação de Melo, será o comparecimento às urnas, já que historicamente o eleitorado que tende a apoiar mais Lula e o PT costuma ter um comparecimento menor. Não à toa, a campanha de Lula vem concentrando esforços em incentivar pessoas que não votaram no primeiro turno a comparecerem na seção eleitoral neste domingo. No primeiro turno, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores não foram votar, uma abstenção de 21,08%, em um total de mais de 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar. Neste domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro também fez um apelo para que os eleitores compareçam às urnas. "Faça chuva ou faça sol, bora sair de casa para votar, que o Brasil vai mudar e o Brasil vai vencer", disse o senador, após votar no Rio de Janeiro, repetindo apelo já feito em suas redes sociais na véspera, em meio à previsão de chuvas fortes nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, onde teve desempenho melhor que Lula. "Chegou a hora da mudança de verdade", afirmou o candidato, ao lado da esposa Fernanda e da mãe, Rogéria. ÔNIBUS Em uma campanha marcada por grande movimentação das duas campanhas contra os adversários no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), que levou o presidente da corte Kassio Nunes Marques a pedir que as campanhas moderassem a quantidade de ações, há receios de que, independentemente do vencedor, ocorram novos embates mesmo após a declaração do resultado. A expectativa de uma margem apertada a favor do eleito também leva a crer que isso possa ocorrer. "A expectativa é de que vai ser uma eleição tensa", disse Creomar de Souza, analista político da Dharma Political Risk. "Acho que a gente ainda vai ter algum nível de discussão política, algum nível de embate jurídico", avaliou. Em meio a essas expectativas, Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais tiveram que agir para sanar problemas no transporte público. O presidente do TRE da Bahia, Mauricio Szporer, [USN:L2N46B04J TEXT:"determinou"] no início da tarde deste domingo a prisão do secretário municipal de Mobilidade de Salvador (Semob), Pablo Souza, sob acusação de ter orientado a redução da frota de ônibus na cidade no dia do segundo turno das eleições. Lula teve mais de 65% dos votos válidos no primeiro turno em Salvador, cujo prefeito, Bruno Reis, é do União Brasil. Em São Paulo, o TRE atendeu a um pedido do PSOL e determinou que a prefeitura colocasse 100% da frota de ônibus para circular neste domingo, com multa de R$100 mil ao prefeito e ao presidente da SPTrans em caso de descumprimento. Em declaração a jornalistas, Lula disse que não aceitaria essa situação. "Não vamos aceitar banditismo e mau-caratismo nem de prefeito, nem de governador", disse o presidente. Ele aproveitou para fazer um apelo que os eleitores não deixem de votar: "Não desistam de votar, esperem e votem". Em entrevista à imprensa, Nunes Marques afirmou que há demanda no TSE para prolongar o período de votação do segundo turno e, sem dar detalhes, disse que "isso certamente, como toda e qualquer ação, será analisado a seu tempo". "De fato, em alguns locais há uma dificuldade ainda no transporte, já está sendo corrigida", disse. Ele acrescentou que o TSE está recebendo, periodicamente, relatórios do TRE da Bahia. DEMOCRACIA E MUDANÇA Eleitores relatavam uma votação sem as filas vistas no primeiro turno, quando foi preciso votar também para deputado federal e estadual, senadores e governador. Neste segundo turno, apenas cinco Estados e o Distrito Federal têm votação para governador, além da eleição para presidente. A bibliotecária aposentada Hilda Corrêa, de 80 anos, fez questão de votar em Brasília, mesmo com o voto não sendo obrigatório a partir dos 70 anos. "Eu exerço essa cidadania minha desde que eu comecei a votar. E eu passei um tempo em que a gente não votava, quando eu era mais jovem, por causa da ditadura... Agora, tem que votar todo tempo. Pela democracia", disse ela, que anunciou voto em Lula. "Ele vai ser muito melhor do que essa turma da bala que está aí." Já o também aposentado José Carlos Jarra, de 61 anos, votou em Flávio Bolsonaro em São Paulo. "A gente precisa da mudança. Eu gostaria que ele (Flávio) mudasse a segurança, olhasse mais pelos aposentados, pelo salário mínimo, que aqui no Brasil é uma vergonha. Também rezo para que o Flávio e o Senado mexam neste Supremo Tribunal Federal", afirmou ele. CAMPANHA ENGRENA As três semanas de campanha do segundo turno foram bastante diferentes dos meses que antecederam o primeiro turno, realizado no dia 4 de outubro. No caso de Lula, uma guinada em direção a uma mobilização maciça nas redes sociais e em eventos de rua. Na véspera da votação, antes de participar de evento de campanha em Copacabana, Lula afirmou que "o povo assumiu para si a responsabilidade de fazer a campanha". Um dos destaques da campanha petista no segundo turno foi o impulso nas redes, liderado pelo canal de WhatsApp "Exército do Lula", criado pelo deputado federal reeleito André Janones (Rede-MG), que juntou mais de 10 milhões de pessoas para ouvir as "missões" que Janones dava para os apoiadores cumprirem nas redes. A campanha de Flávio chegou a entrar no TSE pedindo a suspensão do canal. A guinada digital da campanha petista teve como ápice Lula -- crítico público do uso frequente de celular que se orgulhava de não ter o aparelho -- ganhando um de presente do governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), e passando a fazer vários vídeos no formato selfie para apoiadores. Neste quadro, a Meta (META.O) -- proprietária do Facebook, do Instagram e do WhatsApp -- também ficou no foco, após a campanha de Lula apontar que teve sua atuação restrita nas plataformas da empresa, levando a big tech norte-americana a prestar esclarecimentos ao TSE. Do lado de Flávio, após a inesperada liderança no dia 4, o senador deu declarações que geraram polêmica, como quando disse que, se eleito, usará a força que terá no próximo Congresso para alterar a Constituição. Posteriormente, afirmou que iria propor mudanças constitucionais como o fim da reeleição e a redução da maioridade penal. Também acabou mudando de posição em temas pautados por Lula, como o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, para o qual ele votou favoravelmente no Senado, apesar de, num passado muito recente, ter se declarado contrário. O senador, por outro lado, também conseguiu mobilizar grandes públicos em atos de campanha em todo o país, no que foi uma marca da campanha de ambos os lados. Uma vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro ampliaria uma onda de triunfos de candidatos de direita na América Latina alinhados ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, enquanto um quarto mandato de Lula seria uma decepção para Washington, que teve atritos com o governo do petista em questões de comércio e segurança. Até o momento, Trump evitou declarar apoio a qualquer candidato. Questionado no domingo sobre quem ele gostaria que vencesse, Trump não quis responder. "Não quero entrar nesse assunto, mas estamos acompanhando", disse ele a jornalistas em Washington.

item.title: Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from Congo
item.description: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions. Uganda says it is Ebola-free after [USN:S8N41P031 TEXT:"declaring an end"] to its latest outbreak in July, but there has been concern among health experts after two people who had recently passed through the country later tested positive in [USN:SPN45F00J TEXT:"Kenya"] and [USN:L8N4682IW TEXT:"Nigeria"]. Uganda says it is investigating the Nigerian case, which involves the wife of a Swiss diplomat. The woman, 42, returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa to Abuja on Oct. 3, according to Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control, which said she is in isolation and has improved remarkably. The agency said 53 contacts had been traced. Ugandan officials are reviewing genomic sequencing, travel information, interactions and movements in coordination with Nigerian authorities and international partners. Swiss authorities had said the woman is believed to have contracted the virus in Uganda. Baryomunsi pushed back, saying Switzerland was "speaking prematurely". He said the woman's relatives from West Nile visited her in Kansanga, a suburb of Kampala, and that those relatives had visited Congo. "What evidence do they have that she never travelled there?" he said. "We should speak science, not politics." Kenya's first Ebola patient had travelled from Congo to Uganda and taken a flight from Entebbe airport to Nairobi on Oct. 3. The patient died two days later. Both the Kenyan and the Nigerian cases travelled through the same Ugandan airport on the same day but there was no physical interaction between the two, Diana Atwine, the health ministry's permanent secretary, told the press conference, citing a review of the airport's CCTV system. Baryomunsi said all 60 contacts linked to a [USN:L6N469174 TEXT:"Kenyan Ebola case"] had completed their 21-day monitoring period and been discharged. "The ministry has intensified traveller screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings. All travellers intending to enter Uganda by air, land or water must complete the passenger locator form," he said. [USN:L1N46915U TEXT:"Genomic analysis"] of Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola case showed the virus was closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, though Nigerian authorities said there was no evidence that the Kenya case travelled to Nigeria or had a direct connection. Uganda borders Congo, where the outbreak began, and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks. Late on Sunday, World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a nurse was killed and a health worker severely injured when they were attacked while responding to an Ebola alert in the northern Congolese town of Bafwasende. "Everyone working to protect communities from this deadly disease must be able to work in dignity and safety," he wrote on X, saying the attack occurred on Saturday.

Explainer-How Ukraine’s strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump

Reuters

25 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

By Simon Lewis and Steve Holland WASHINGTON, Oct 25 (Reuters) – Relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticizing the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward.

Here’s how the relationship soured:

WHAT IS THE HISTORY OF TRUMP-ZELENSKIY TENSIONS?

Show Full Article

Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv.

“Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.”

Trump’s first major encounter with Zelenskiy came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorized.

That episode led to Trump’s first impeachment. Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election.

Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un.

“Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said.

WHAT DEEPENED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE TWO LEADERS?

Trump’s current frustration centers on Kyiv’s attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure.

Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump’s Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

On September 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments.

Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages.

Angered by Zelenskiy’s defiance, Trump on October 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorized by a bill he signed into law in September.

Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an energy ceasefire on October 11.

“It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage,” said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank.

HAS THE US THREATENED TO CUT OFF SUPPORT TO UKRAINE?

Zelenskiy has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv’s account.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine.

“We don’t have to pressure Zelenskiy. If he wants to make a deal he’ll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelenskiy) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn’t seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit.”

On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company’s Starlink satellite system. Starlink’s disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv’s military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenseless against Russia’s attacks going into the winter.

WHAT IS THE STATUS OF MOSCOW-KYIV PEACE TALKS?

Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results.

At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump’s demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries.

The next day, envoy Witkoff – a close friend of Trump’s – met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture.

Zelenskiy said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

(Reporting by Steve Holland and Simon Lewis; Editing by Don Durfee and David Gregorio)
